title: Molecular structures and quantum chemistry, in view
description: Explore molecular orbitals and electron density, customize surfaces with live shaders, and inspect large molecular structures in EigenVista.
text: Orbitals / electron density / custom shaders / AI-enabled Quantum chemistry. In view. Explore the field. Reveal the molecule. Shape the view with custom surface shaders and live controls. 0.10.5 · Available for Mac and Linux. Color proteins by residue class and use X-ray shading that follows the assigned surface color. Explore residue coloring → Both downloads include this workspace, the scientific tools and the AI connector. ✦ AI-enabled viewing → Ask your coding agent to explore molecules, prepare surfaces and export figures. Included in EigenVista 0.10.5 for Mac and Linux. Download for Mac ↗ Download for Linux ↗ Explore surface shaders → Published downloads: v0.10.5 · Apple Silicon Mac / Linux x86_64 · Experimental preview Mac: ad-hoc signed; not notarized. Linux: tested on CachyOS; check the runtime requirements. Installation notes 01 / X-RAY SURFACE SHADER C₇H₁₀ Electron density at 0.04 electrons/bohr³ on a 256³ grid. The X-ray shader reveals the 17-atom framework inside the surface. Make this view → MOLDEN PDB mmCIF / BCIF XYZ CUBE .EIGENVISTA Four tabs / one workspace Read the field. Keep the numbers. A true plane through the HOMO, with signed values, contours and a numerical colorbar. Choose Fields → Quantitative field inspection to probe a point, sample a section or plot a bond profile. The C₇H₁₀ HOMO sampled on a real plane. Blue and red encode the sign of orbital amplitude ψ, not charge; the key spans −0.06 to +0.06 bohr⁻³ᐟ². Total electron density is a separate nonnegative field. Actual 0.9.0 source-preview capture, 17 November 2026; this pane design became the default in 0.10.0 and is retained in EigenVista 0.10.5. Capture provenance . Move the 480 px pane left or right, resize it, and collapse or reorder familiar widgets inside Molecule, Fields, Surfaces and Appearance. Hide Tools to reclaim the scene, or use Zen for a minimal view with the field's numerical key still visible. Make a quantitative section → Tour the new workspace → Watch / 30 seconds One density. Three ways to see it. From a solid molecular envelope to X-ray transparency and a moving clipping boundary. Watch the controls redraw the same density mesh. Download the shader demonstration (MP4) . Actual EigenVista 0.7.2 recording. The C₇H₁₀ electron density is sampled on a 256³ grid at 0.04 electrons/bohr³. Changing opacity and clipping parameters reuses that mesh. English narration with captions; a text description is available below. Read the demonstration description The solid density envelope surrounds the bicyclic hydrocarbon. Applying the X-ray shader reveals the atoms beneath; adjusting maxOpacity changes the transparency immediately. The clipping shader then removes the part of the envelope beyond a boundary. Changing zmax moves that boundary through the surface and exposes the molecular framework. The underlying density and isovalue remain the same throughout. Recreate these views → Download video ↓ 01 / Explore From the calculation. Into the scene. [01] Choose the orbital Browse orbital energies, occupations and spin. Inspect signed isosurfaces, explore a volume, or compare fields from a Molden file. Orbitals and density → [02] Make the surface yours Load a custom shader and tune its controls as you look. Reveal an interior with X-ray opacity, clip a surface, or change its lighting. Surface shaders → [03] Read the molecule Move between atomic detail and protein cartoons. Color by element or chain, isolate a region, and use ambient occlusion to reveal depth in dense structures. Molecular representations → 02 / CLIPPING SHADER THE SAME DENSITY The same 0.04 electrons/bohr³ density surface, opened with a clipping shader. Adjust the boundary with a live parameter. 02 / Custom surface shaders One surface. Your way in. Change the lighting, reveal the framework through a translucent envelope, or move a clipping boundary through the molecule. Shader parameters redraw the existing mesh immediately. Start with the supplied presets. Load the vertex and fragment files, then adjust the controls in Surface shader . Save a parameter file when you find a look you want to use again. Try the shader presets → 03 / FRONTIER ORBITALS MO 27 / LUMO The C₇H₁₀ LUMO (MO 27), with signed isosurfaces at ±0.03 bohr −3/2 . The two colors identify the sign of the orbital amplitude. 03 / Molecular orbitals Follow the lobes. Compare the orbitals. Choose among the 118 orbitals in this bicyclic hydrocarbon example. Compare the HOMO and LUMO, inspect their nodal structure, and switch between a saved mesh and a volume preview. Generate a fine grid when you want a detailed surface. Calculations run in the background, with progress and cancellation available while you explore the scene. Explore the orbital workflow → 04 / Large molecular structures Find the folds. Ambient occlusion brings contacts, recesses and broad cavities into view. Try the Pastel palette for atoms and bonds, or shade an opaque SES or SAS with its own controls. AO OFF AO ON Reveal ambient occlusion 50% 1AON: 58,870 atoms, with the same camera, structure and MatterViz Pastel element palette. Off uses normal shading; On uses Lambert + SSAO. Recreate this view → SES ambient occlusion Bring out pockets and clefts on the solvent-excluded surface of the same 1AON complex. Try it on a molecular surface → AO OFF AO ON Reveal molecular surface AO 50% Full 1AON SES, 4.18 million triangles, from the same camera. Alvarez radii, 1.4 Å probe, 0.5 Å grid spacing and 24 Å automatic AO radius. Download 1AON . 05 / A CONVERSATION WITH THE VIEWER RECORDED SESSION An actual external-agent session: the C₇H₁₀ HOMO at ±0.03 bohr −3/2 , refined from 64³ to 128³ and styled with the X-ray preset. 05 / AI-assisted viewing Ask for the view. Inspect the result. Use Codex, Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode or another coding agent to open molecular data, find orbitals, prepare surfaces and export figures. You describe the task in your agent's chat while EigenVista shows the result. EigenVista 0.10.5 for Mac and Linux includes its prebuilt connection helper, launcher, examples and agent instructions. No source checkout or compiler is needed for the binary setup. Meet the AI connector → Follow a real session → From data to figure Keep the result. Share the view. Save molecular data and generated meshes together in an .eigenvista document. Export the current view as a PNG, including a transparent-background option for figures and presentations. Install EigenVista → Choose a tutorial → Browse the gallery →

title: Install & start
description: Download EigenVista for Apple Silicon Mac or CachyOS-tested Linux x86_64, install the desktop app and open the supplied molecular examples.
text: On this page Download Requirements Install on Mac Install on Linux First run In the package Troubleshooting Get EigenVista 0.10.5 An experimental desktop preview for Apple Silicon Macs and CachyOS-tested Linux x86_64. Your local molecular-file workflows run on your computer, without a calculation server. Published download: 0.10.5. Both packages include the four-tab Tools pane, scientific-inspection controls and AI connector described in this manual. It retains clearer action buttons, visible atom picks, automatic field-plane updates and molecular-surface progress. Version 0.10.5 also includes pending-edit Save coordination, optional replacement for ExFAT exports and the Accessible elements palette. These installation and first-run steps apply to the 0.10.5 package. MAC / APPLE SILICON / v0.10.5 Download the tester ZIP ↗ 83.1 MB · Includes the application, AI connector, examples, palettes and converter. SHA-256 checksum Build information Release notes LINUX / X86_64 / v0.10.5 Download for Linux ↗ 83.6 MB · CachyOS-tested desktop app, AI connector, examples, palettes and converter. Linux SHA-256 checksum Linux build information Linux installation steps Before you download Apple Silicon Mac: an M-series processor. This ZIP does not run on Intel Macs. macOS 13 or later is the deployment target. The release was built and checked locally on macOS 27; the full supported OS range has not been qualified. Linux x86_64: the CachyOS-tested archive uses system GTK 3 and WebKitGTK 4.1. Check its runtime and display requirements . Windows and Intel Mac packages are not available. The installed app needs no Rust, Node.js, development server or internet connection to work with local files. Development preview. The Mac app is ad-hoc signed and is not Apple-notarized. Follow the macOS instructions below when opening it for the first time. Install on your Mac Download and unzip the complete tester package. Move EigenVista.app into Applications . Double-click the app. It initially opens a mathematical hydrogen-pair example. Keep the rest of the extracted package: it contains examples, palettes, documentation, source and license notices. If macOS asks about the developer Only proceed when you trust the download's origin and integrity. After trying to open the app, go to System Settings → Privacy Security → Open Anyway , then confirm Open for EigenVista. Managed Macs may prevent this exception. Do not disable Gatekeeper globally. Stop and report malware or damaged-app warnings instead of bypassing them. Apple explains these security messages ↗ . Optionally verify the ZIP checksum The companion checksum detects download corruption; it does not authenticate a publisher by itself. In Terminal, in the folder containing both downloaded files: shasum -a 256 -c EigenVista-0.10.5-apple-silicon-20261123T032216Z-b6a3f27.zip.sha256 The result should end in OK . The ZIP's SHA-256 is: 21ed61775bdfb8af273d249a57662b939a7b34b28ed90a4609bd5b0371294bff Install on Linux This x86_64 archive was built and tested on CachyOS , with glibc 2.44 , GTK 3 and WebKitGTK 4.1 version 2.54.1 . It uses those system libraries. It is not an AppImage, and compatibility with older glibc or another distribution has not been established. You need a graphical Linux session with WebGL2. The native app was tested on an isolated X11 display; physical desktop/file-dialog behavior, Wayland and native hardware GPU operation still need qualification. An SSH connection alone does not provide a display. The standalone converter can run without one. Download the complete Linux archive and its checksum into the same folder. On CachyOS/Arch, install the runtime libraries through your normal signed package-manager workflow. Keep your distribution repositories consistent: sudo pacman -S --needed webkit2gtk-4.1 gtk3 openssl In Terminal, in the folder containing your downloads, verify and extract the archive. These commands work in Fish as well as Bash: sha256sum -c EigenVista-0.10.5-linux-x86_64-20261123T032215Z-b6a3f27.tar.gz.sha256 tar -xzf EigenVista-0.10.5-linux-x86_64-20261123T032215Z-b6a3f27.tar.gz cd EigenVista-0.10.5-linux-x86_64-20261123T032215Z-b6a3f27 ./bin/eigenvista The checksum result should end in OK . The Linux archive's SHA-256 is: cce546de5b3f4b34a8701c6501be59634368dcbf36418d02b8afc0816215ae3f Keep bin/ and share/ together. The examples are in share/eigenvista/Examples/ ; palettes and shader presets are beside them. No Rust compiler, Node.js, development server or source checkout is needed to run the installed app. Linux item Purpose bin/eigenvista The desktop viewer. bin/eigenvista-ctl The prebuilt connection helper used by your AI agent. bin/eigenvista-convert Optional command-line conversion without a graphical display. share/eigenvista/AI-connector/ The Bash launcher, standalone instructions, examples and palettes. share/eigenvista/ Examples, palettes, shaders, offline guides, notices and exact source/dependency archives. For a connected session, follow the Linux AI setup steps . You can keep the extracted package in any directory you own; no system-wide application installation is required. If the Linux app cannot start Check that you downloaded the x86_64 package, installed GTK/WebKitGTK runtime dependencies and launched it inside a graphical session. Missing-library or GLIBC_… not found errors indicate a runtime mismatch. Do not replace system libraries with copies from another distribution. Report the distribution, package version, display type and full error with the build-information file . Other distributions need their own compatible build and testing. Check your first session The 0.10.5 app uses one resizable Tools pane. Find structure controls under Molecule , quantum rendering and numerical inspection under Fields , shape/meshes under Surfaces , and palettes/AO/shaders under Appearance . Move the pane left or right, resize it or hide it; Zen gives the view almost the whole window. See the workspace guide . On Linux, use the examples inside share/eigenvista/Examples/ . On Mac, use the package's top-level Examples/ folder. Use the app's Open button and choose Examples/water.pdb . Molecular data should show 3 atoms and 2 bonds . Display bonds are computed automatically. Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, or use the toolbar's Zoom in and Zoom out buttons. Fit scene brings the molecule back into view. Choose Van der Waals for space-filling spheres, then return to Ball and stick . Save to a new .eigenvista file and reopen it with Open . To try orbital and density rendering, open Examples/water.molden with the app’s Open button. To operate the viewer through Codex, Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode or another coding agent, follow AI connection setup ; the connection tools are already included in your package. Next Your first molecule → Explore a supplied orbital → What is in the Mac ZIP? Item Purpose EigenVista.app The desktop viewer, with its AI connection helper, launcher, instructions, examples and palettes inside the app. Examples/ Water PDB/XYZ, a calculated water Molden file and a synthetic signed cube. Palettes/ Accessible elements, MatterViz Muted and MatterViz Pastel JSON files, loading instructions and palette notices. Tools/eigenvista-convert Optional command-line conversion without a GUI. Shaders/ Optional surface-shader examples and attribution. Guides, notices and source Offline instructions, source snapshots, license notices and build information. If something does not look right No quantum fields after opening a structure Open a Molden file for orbitals and densities, or a cube file for a sampled scalar field. See supported formats . A blank or distant scene Use Fit scene . For sampled fields, inspect the field range and adjust the isovalue; a warning about unknown cube units does not remove the sampled field. Navigation is slow Turn off ambient occlusion, use a simpler representation or lower preview quality. A finer grid costs memory and computation; it is not always a better first view. A graphics-context error Reload or restart after a lost context. Retain original molecular inputs and save useful work regularly. Need help? Report the file type, app version, operating-system version and steps on GitHub ↗ . Only attach calculation files you are allowed to share.

title: User reference
description: The EigenVista 0.10.5 manual: files, scene controls, quantum fields, scientific inspection, biological structures, and saving.
text: EigenVista displays molecular structures and supplied quantum-chemistry fields in an interactive 3D scene. This reference covers EigenVista 0.10.5 , including the four-tab workspace and scientific inspection . The 0.10.5 Mac download includes these tools and its AI connector. Start with the installation guide or a worked tutorial with a downloadable example. New in 0.10.5: opaque SES and SAS can use matte screen-space ambient occlusion. The radius scales with the molecule. Shade a molecular surface → Find a workflow Files, imports, conversion, and saving — choose a format, review import decisions, use the batch converter, and share a self-contained document. Scene, appearance, and images — navigate, pick atoms, choose a representation, use ambient occlusion and palettes, export PNGs, or apply a surface shader. Custom surface shaders — see through a density envelope, expose its interior with clipping, and tune lighting and transparency live. Orbitals, densities, and sampled fields — generate signed surfaces, browse several orbitals, compare render modes, and understand resolution and caching. Biological structures — color chains and secondary structure, show components, isolate a chain, select residue ranges, and use protein depictions. AI-assisted viewing — connect your external coding agent, describe a molecular view, and keep exported figures and native documents. Scientific inspection — 0.10.5 — measurements and labels, ligand neighborhoods, SES/SAS shape, numerical probes, planes/contours and profiles. The application workspace One Tools pane starts on the right at 480 px wide. Its four tabs are inside the pane; choose Position → Left to move it across the scene. Drag the inner divider to resize it. The existing header, file buttons, viewport toolbar and footer stay in their familiar places. Area What you do there Top bar Read the document title and unsaved indicator; choose Open , Convert , or Save . Three compact buttons show/hide Tools, enter Zen and toggle fullscreen. Molecule tab Molecular data : counts, representation and biological controls. Selections and measurements : ordered picks, named sets, labels and neighborhoods. Provenance : source decisions and warnings. Fields tab Quantum fields : orbitals, densities and sampled fields. Field rendering : volume/raycast, isovalue, resolution and mesh generation. Quantitative field inspection : probes, true planes, contours and line profiles. Surfaces tab Molecular surfaces : coordinate-derived SES/SAS and live saved appearance. Saved surfaces : quantum/imported mesh visibility and triangle counts. Appearance tab Appearance : field colors/opacity, surface shading and molecular AO. Atom colours : element palettes. Surface shader : custom GLSL sources, targets and live parameters. Central scene Rotate, pan, zoom, and pick an atom or saved surface. Inspection information appears below the scene. Footer and progress panel Read operation status, completed sampling slices, signed meshing passes, elapsed time, and errors. Close Tools to give its width back to the scene. The header's Show tools button or Shift+T brings back the same pane. At narrow widths it overlays the scene instead of squeezing it. Switching tabs, changing side or hiding the pane retains tool drafts and the current camera; a hidden pane does not cancel a calculation. Fields → Quantitative field inspection beside a true C₇H₁₀ HOMO section. The orbital amplitude ψ has both signs; its blue–white–red key spans −0.06 to +0.06 bohr⁻³ᐟ², with contours on the sampled plane. Actual 0.9.0 source-preview capture, 17 November 2026; this pane design became the default in 0.10.0 and is retained in EigenVista 0.10.5. Capture provenance . Keyboard and widget controls Use Tab to move between controls and Enter or Space to activate buttons. Left/Right and Home/End move among the four pane tabs. A widget heading is a button: activate it to collapse or expand that section. Collapsing retains settings and selections. In Safari on macOS, use Option-Tab if ordinary Tab skips buttons, or enable macOS Keyboard Navigation. To move a widget, drag its Reorder handle onto the upper or lower half of another heading in the same tab. Alternatively, click or tap the handle and choose Move up or Move down . With keyboard focus on the handle, use Up/Down to move one place, or Home/End to move to the start/end of that tab's stack. Focus stays on the handle and the new position is announced. Escape closes the move controls and returns focus to the handle. Widget order stays within its tab. Pane side, width, active tab and visibility are profile preferences, alongside widget order/expansion; they are not part of a molecular document. Without profile storage they last for the session. On the focused divider, use Left/Right, Shift+arrows for a larger step, or Home/End to resize. Closing a widget differs from closing the whole pane: only closing the pane reclaims its scene width. Shift+Z enters Zen: header, footer and Tools hide while Exit Zen, Tools, source identity and essential scene controls remain. Choose Tools to leave Zen and reopen the pane. Fullscreen is separate and uses the browser's actual facility. While fullscreen is active the platform handles Escape first; after leaving fullscreen, Escape can leave Zen. Visible exits remain available. Shortcuts leave editable inputs and modal dialogs alone. The orbital browser remains a modal chooser. Progress and Cancel calculation remain available outside the pane, including in Zen, for cancellable work. Hiding Tools or switching tabs neither restarts nor cancels it. A noncancellable Save shows status without a misleading Cancel action. Browser fullscreen does not establish native macOS fullscreen or multi-monitor qualification. The scene's Zoom in , Zoom out , Fit scene , and Reset view buttons provide alternatives to mouse gestures. See scene navigation . What is saved? Save writes the molecular document. It does not capture every view preference. The phrase Saved surfaces means meshes in the current document's memory; they reach disk only when you save the document. Kind of state Examples After reopening or restarting Saved molecular data Atoms and biological identities, bonds, supplied basis/orbitals/density matrices or original sampled grids, provenance, saved meshes, named selections, measurements/labels and quantitative analysis definitions/caches. Retained in .eigenvista by a matching current build. Saved document appearance Global molecular representation, surface colors, opacity, and saved-mesh visibility. Retained in .eigenvista . Session display settings Camera, render mode, background, AO, atom palette, surface shading, shader/uniforms, preview quality, biological filters/styles, orbital checkboxes, and preview sampling cache. Not stored in the molecular file. Reapply after restarting; some settings continue across Open within a session. Profile preferences Pane side, width, active tab and visibility; per-tab widget order and expansion. Remembered on that browser/desktop profile when storage is available; not shared with the document. Zen is transient. Each mesh records the grid used to generate it, but the Grid resolution control resets in a new application session. Generated orbital/density grids are transient; their analytic inputs and saved meshes persist. Imported cube grids retain their original values. See saving and sharing and field caching . When something looks wrong Symptom Next step Generate surfaces is disabled Select an orbital, density matrix, or sampled field in Quantum fields . Wait for another active operation to finish or cancel it. Generate selected is disabled Check between 1 and 32 orbitals and enter a finite positive isovalue. Raycast/volume choices are disabled Select an available field and finish/cancel other active work. Analytic orbital/density previews do not require meshes. No field appears Use Fit scene , check the selected mode and field, and try a smaller positive isovalue. Read any preview error. An all-zero field has no nonzero surface. A structure seems missing Fit the scene, try Ball and stick , and check counts and biological visibility filters. Show all components clears those filters. Atom/bond counts differ from the source Read Provenance : model, alternate, occupancy, unknown-element, declared-connection, and inferred-bond policies can change the selected display structure. A calculation is slow or memory allocation fails Read the phase, counts and elapsed time. Cancel if needed. If the computer cannot allocate the requested data, retry with fewer orbitals, a lower grid resolution or a smaller explicit selection. Existing completed results are retained on recoverable errors. Volume changes unexpectedly with quality Use 0.5.14 or later; earlier builds had an opacity/quality interaction. In all versions, volume intersections with opaque objects remain approximate. A file is rejected Read the exact error and supported profile. Export an appropriate supported file rather than removing producer, units, or validation markers. WebGL2 is unavailable / graphics context lost Check graphics acceleration. A lost context requires restart/reload; save if possible beforehand. Unsaved data can be lost. See supported file formats for import options and rendering limits for guidance on sampled previews and transparency. For a problem report , include the package filename or BUILD-INFO.json , Mac model/processor, OS version, exact error, steps, and a screenshot. Share a small input only if you have permission to publish it. Keep confidential research data out of public issues.

title: Files, conversion, and saving
description: Open Molden, Gaussian Cube, PDB, mmCIF, BinaryCIF and XYZ files; inspect import provenance, batch-convert inputs, and save native EigenVista documents.
text: This guide follows EigenVista 0.10.5. Use the four tabs in the single Tools pane: Molecule, Fields, Surfaces and Appearance. The 0.10.5 Mac package includes this workspace and all the scientific-inspection tools described here. Find your way around the current workspace → Open an existing calculation or structure, inspect the import report, and save a self-contained .eigenvista document. Opening never overwrites the input. Keep original files: the preview deliberately imports a selected, supported subset rather than every source annotation. Open and check a file Choose Open in the app's top bar, then select a supported local file. Use this button: Finder file associations and drag-and-drop loading are not implemented. If prompted about unsaved work, save or deliberately discard it before replacing the scene. Check counts under Molecule → Molecular data and Fields → Quantum fields . Read Import report and Molecule → Provenance , including warnings. Use Fit scene if necessary. Imported structures show automatic display bonds; cube fields normally start in Volume preview . Choose Save and a new .eigenvista filename to retain the imported data and subsequent changes. External imports start unsaved. A malformed-file error leaves the previous document intact. A valid grid that exceeds rendering precision can still open and remain savable with a preview error; see grid precision . The installed app performs these local workflows without an internet connection. For a small structure check, download water.xyz : it should show 3 atoms and 2 bonds . For quantum fields, try water.molden ; for a sampled field, try signed-affine.cube . Supported formats Input What it supplies Supported boundary .eigenvista , .molekel Rust-preview scientific document, saved appearance, and meshes. Current and supported earlier preview formats. Not a general project reader for the old C++ Molekel application. Molden: .molden , .molf , .molden.input , or recognized header Geometry, Gaussian basis, real orbitals, energies, occupations, and eligible occupation-derived density matrices. One geometry and basis; canonical S/P/D/F/G and SP. Identified ORCA exports have a narrower qualified subset. .xyz Geometry in angstroms and inferred display bonds. One conventional atom-count/comment/coordinate frame. Extra columns, extended XYZ, and multiple frames are rejected. .pdb Selected ATOM/HETATM geometry, supported biological metadata, explicit and inferred bonds. First model/structure and one alternate conformer per residue. .cif , .mcif , .pdbx Selected mmCIF atom sites, biological metadata, declared connections, and inferred bonds. Bounded mmCIF profile; first model/alternate policy. No crystal-image expansion or complete dictionary validation. .bcif , .bcif.gz The same selected structure and connection policy as text mmCIF. BinaryCIF 0.3.x, one data block; raw or gzip-wrapped content. Gzip support does not extend to text mmCIF or PDB. .cube , .cub Atoms, automatic bonds, and one already sampled scalar field. Supported bohr-coordinate profile, including a single-orbital dataset header. No multi-field or alternative-unit cube profile. OBJ, legacy atom-color text formats, direct ORCA output/GBW, and Gaussian logs are not implemented. Atom palettes use the separate JSON palette picker . For biological selection, identities, and omitted annotations, see structure import policy . For exact accepted cube features and what a sampled field means, see cube fields . EigenVista does not impose fixed file-byte, atom or bond quotas. Import attempts to allocate the required data and reports allocation failures or values that cannot be represented. Supported format profiles and scientific validation still apply. Large files can take longer to read and display; see memory and precision . Molden wavefunctions and density interpretation A supported Molden input supplies one [Atoms] section with explicit AU or Angs units, one [GTO] basis, and real orbitals in one or more [MO] sections. Missing geometry/basis, ambiguous repeated sections, unsupported shell conventions, or invalid coefficients are errors. The reader does not repair an unrecognized producer convention by guessing. Imported orbital labels include supplied symmetry information. Energies use hartree. Missing energies or occupations remain missing; an explicit Alpha/Beta spin is required by the Molden profile. One Alpha-only set is interpreted and reported as spatial orbitals with occupations up to two. Mixed Alpha/Beta sets retain their spin labels with occupations up to one; fractional occupations are preserved. Where the density comes from If every listed orbital has an occupation, the importer constructs the occupation-weighted density from those listed coefficients. A spatial set provides a total-kind matrix; a mixed Alpha/Beta set additionally provides alpha, beta, total, and alpha-minus-beta spin matrices. A beta-only set remains beta-only. If any occupation is missing, no derived density is created. Fields labelled Occupation-derived … (listed orbitals) describe the listed export. They are not recovered correlated, transition, or independent difference density matrices. A truncated orbital set can produce only a partial density; omitted orbitals and ECP core electrons are not recovered. Zero-occupation virtual orbitals remain fully validated, listed, renderable, and savable. They contribute zero to the derived density. A fractional nonzero occupation contributes its supplied value. The initial field is the last source-order orbital with positive occupation, or the first orbital if none qualifies; unusual ordering means this is not necessarily the highest-energy orbital. ORCA exports Export a Molden file with ORCA's orca_2mkl before opening it. Preserve the producer title/marker: it selects the normalization convention. The qualified subset currently accepts S, P, and spherical 5D shells; ORCA SP, Cartesian D, F, and G are rejected. This is not a claim of support for every ORCA version or option. Do not remove a producer marker to bypass rejection. Frequency, normal-mode, optimization-trajectory, charge, and core/ECP sections are not preserved as structured data. Ignored sections are named in the report. Keep the original calculation. A supported file needs no installed Python, ORCA, or other calculation program to be read. The downloadable water example is a calculated RHF wavefunction with 24 basis functions, 24 spatial orbitals, and a total density . Follow the orbital tutorial to inspect it. Read import warnings and provenance The import report summarizes what was accepted and what needs attention. Provenance retains source information and decisions in the native document: original input name and byte checksum, importer/profile identification, bond method, warnings, and reported omissions. A checksum identifies source bytes; it is not a certification that the source's chemistry is correct. The source file itself is not embedded wholesale. For structures, look for model/alternate selection, omitted zero-occupancy or unknown-element rows, missing/ambiguous identities, secondary-structure notices, and connection decisions. mmCIF/BinaryCIF declared connections retain deposited references, type/order, resolved selected endpoints, and retained/duplicate/omitted status. Cell/symmetry information is reported without creating symmetry mates. A compressed BinaryCIF checksum identifies the actual compressed input bytes. All supported imports compute display bonds automatically. PDB CONECT and supported mmCIF covalent, disulfide, and metal declarations take precedence and are supplemented by coordinate-based connections. Rods represent display connectivity; they do not establish bond order, aromaticity, hydrogen bonds, oxidation state, or chemical validity. When opening an older native document, missing display bonds may be added while preserving existing connections, scientific arrays, and meshes. The addition is reported and the document becomes unsaved. Save explicitly to retain the change; Open leaves the original untouched. Convert files without replacing the scene Choose Convert files . The separate Convert Files window leaves the current scene open. Add supported input files and click Convert . Files are processed sequentially. Review each row's report. A failed row shows its own error and does not discard successful results. Click a successful row's Save . Desktop Save opens a destination dialog; browser Save requests a download. Conversion alone writes nothing. Save completed results when ready. Clear results you no longer need to release their memory. Cancel stops that queue's pending work and retains completed results. Closing the conversion window preserves them in memory; Clear discards them. Saved/downloaded result bytes are released. Unwritten results do not survive closing the application. Conversion preserves supplied fields and existing native meshes but does not generate new surfaces. Save, reopen, and share Save creates a self-contained .eigenvista file containing selected structure and biological identities when available, bonds, supplied analytic fields or original sampled grids, provenance, saved surface geometry and generation metadata, visibility, colors, opacity, and global representation. Since 0.10.0, this also includes named selections, labels/measurements, SES/SAS meshes and accepted quantitative field definitions/caches. A matching installation can reopen results without their original inputs or silent recalculation; older 0.8.0 readers cannot open documents requiring these newer capabilities. Save coordination in 0.10.3: Save refuses while an inspection edit is still being applied. Wait for the edit to finish, then save again. This includes committed plane changes during their brief update delay, surface appearance and annotations; typing an uncommitted draft does not block Save. Earlier packages, including 0.10.2, predate this correction. Generate any meshes you want to keep, check visibility and appearance, and choose Save . On desktop, choose a destination. Cancelling leaves the document unsaved. In a browser, confirm the requested download completed. Reopen the saved file with Open . Existing meshes start in Isosurface mesh mode. The camera, active render mode, and session preferences are not restored. Share that file with another compatible preview installation. Keep the original input and a backup because the preview schema is not frozen. Save does not export back to Molden, PDB, XYZ, mmCIF, or cube. There is no separate OBJ-plus-metadata export or external mesh linking. There is no automatic background saving, undo for surface deletion, or crash recovery. Use different native filenames to preserve multiple isovalues of the same field; regenerating replaces that field's meshes. Compatibility and filesystem details Older Rust-preview .molekel files open without a manual migration. Native Save also accepts that suffix, but new saves contain EigenVista identifiers regardless of filename and are not guaranteed to open in earlier Molekel builds. Native files containing biological identities require an application that supports the biological-structure feature. Keep an original when older software must continue to read it. Desktop Save publishes a complete replacement file. On the tested APFS volume, replacing an existing file sets permissions to 0600 (owner read/write). Atomic replacement does not establish recovery after a crash or power loss. Default converter/AI exports refuse overwrites; the tested Mac ExFAT driver cannot provide that publication mode. In 0.10.3, an explicitly selected replacement mode permits complete atomic exports on that volume, including over existing or late-created destinations. Imported source files remain protected. Use replacement only when intentional. Older converters lack this option; create their output on APFS and copy the completed file instead. Other filesystem/platform behavior is not broadly qualified. Leaving the application Desktop close/quit checks for unsaved changes, unfinished operations, and converted results awaiting Save. Choose Cancel to continue working, Discard and Quit to cancel work and leave without saving, or Save and Quit to save the current document before leaving. Failed or cancelled saves keep the document open. Review a refreshed prompt if the document changes while it is displayed. Finish/cancel an existing native save first; save converted results from their queue. Save and Quit is unavailable while the queue has unfinished or unsaved work. Browsers use their own close warning. Confirm all downloads before closing. When sharing the application, forward the complete tester ZIP with licenses, notices, and Source. Command-line converter The tester ZIP contains Tools/eigenvista-convert . The following examples assume it is on your PATH. Create output directories first. The converter supports the same input profiles as Open, including mmCIF/BinaryCIF and cube. eigenvista-convert calculation.molden eigenvista-convert calculation.molden.input --output calculation.eigenvista eigenvista-convert --output-dir converted water.molden structure.cif eigenvista-convert --check --json calculation.cube eigenvista-convert --help A single input defaults to a sibling .eigenvista output; multiple inputs require --output-dir . --output (or -o ) chooses one destination. --check validates and reports without writing. --json writes per-file results, counts, warnings, and errors as an array on standard output; otherwise summaries go to standard error. Use -- before filenames beginning with a hyphen. Existing outputs require explicit permission. --force keeps its earlier behavior: permission applies to an output that exists at preflight. Initially absent outputs still use no-clobber publication even with force and require filesystem hard-link support; unsupported publication is an error, not a partial-write fallback. Version 0.10.3 adds --replace for atomic replacement, including on the tested Mac ExFAT volume. This option may replace a destination created during conversion; choose it only when that is acceptable. It cannot be combined with --force or --check . An input can never be its own destination. The converter rejects colliding destinations and output symlinks. Inputs are processed sequentially. Later per-file failures retain successful outputs. Exit status is 0 for complete success, 1 for a per-file import/write failure, and 2 for invalid options or path preflight errors. Conversion creates no new meshes. Open its output in the app, generate surfaces, and Save when you need portable geometry.

title: Scene, appearance, and images
description: Camera and picking controls, molecular representations, Pastel palettes, ambient occlusion, PNG exports, and surface shaders.
text: This guide follows EigenVista 0.10.5. Use the four tabs in the single Tools pane: Molecule, Fields, Surfaces and Appearance. The 0.10.5 Mac package includes this workspace and all the scientific-inspection tools described here. Find your way around the current workspace → Frame a molecule, choose how atoms and fields are drawn, then export the current viewport. Global representation and field colors/opacity belong to the document. Camera, background, lighting choices, palettes, and shaders are display preferences for the session. Navigate and inspect Action Control Rotate Left-drag; one-finger drag on a touchscreen. Pan Right-drag or Ctrl-drag; two-finger pan on a touchscreen. Zoom Scroll, or middle-button drag vertically; pinch on a touchscreen. The toolbar also has Zoom in and Zoom out . Restore framing Fit scene or Reset view . Both currently fit all displayed objects and restore the default viewing direction. Inspect an atom Click it to show element, index, and coordinates in angstroms. Biological context appears alongside when supplied. Inspect a saved mesh Click it to show its label and triangle count. Tab to toolbar buttons and activate with Enter or Space. Hover an icon to read its name. The app displays picked information and supports distance, angle and signed-torsion measurements . Neither modifies molecular coordinates. The camera is not saved in .eigenvista . Molecular representations Choose Representation in Molecule → Molecular data . The global choice is saved with the document. Choice Depiction and use Ball and stick Atoms and connecting rods; useful for checking a small structure and its display connectivity. Liquorice A rod-focused atomic view for inspecting connected molecular detail. Van der Waals Space-filling atom spheres; no bond cylinders. Useful with ambient occlusion for dense molecules. Protein backbone trace A path through supported protein backbone points. Protein smooth tube A smoother tube following the supported backbone. Protein ribbon Oriented protein ribbons where deposited identities and backbone geometry permit. Protein cartoon Helical ribbons, strand arrows, and connecting loops based on deposited secondary assignments. Protein choices require suitable biological identities. Nonprotein components retain atomic detail; chain/component overrides can mix styles. Missing atoms and gaps break protein paths rather than inventing a connection. See protein depiction rules . Element colors cover atomic numbers 1–118. Display radii use published van der Waals tables where available and a covalent-radius-based continuation for Fm–Og; they are visual models. Automatic bonds use a separate covalent-radius heuristic. A drawn rod is not a bond-order or chemical-validity result. Field colors, opacity, and surface shading Under Appearance , Positive and Negative choose signed field colors, and Opacity controls field transparency. These apply across quantum/imported-field surfaces, not just the selected field, and are retained when saved. Molecular SES/SAS has its own live saved color and opacity under Surfaces → Molecular surfaces . Appearance edits do not recompute either field or geometry. Surface shading offers Diffuse (the default) and Blinn-Phong (specular highlights on saved meshes and sampled raycast isosurfaces). It is a session preference, separate from atom/bond materials, and is not stored in the molecular document. Choose the rendering mode under Field rendering. A single camera-aligned light and neutral fill give a smooth shape gradient as you orbit, pan or roll. Every viewing direction uses the same lighting, without opposing-light bands or repeated highlight spots. Atoms, bonds, protein depictions and built-in mesh/raycast surfaces share this arrangement. Blinn-Phong adds one coherent specular highlight; Diffuse keeps the built-in surface matte. Custom shaders keep their declared lighting; volume compositing stays unlit. In Surfaces → Saved surfaces , the eye icon toggles one mesh's visibility and the trash icon removes it. There is no undo. Save to retain those changes. In sampled modes, the active field's meshes are visually replaced by the sampled display; eye/trash controls still manage saved meshes. Return to Isosurface mesh to inspect their effect independently. Molecular ambient occlusion Ambient occlusion emphasizes atom contacts and broad recesses in dense molecules. It starts off. While enabled with nonzero strength, atoms and bonds use Lambert shading plus screen-space ambient occlusion (SSAO) , without specular highlights. For space-filling detail, choose Representation → Van der Waals . For best results, download matterviz-pastel.json and load it through Appearance → Atom colours → Colours file… . For a biological structure, choose Coloring → Element to see that palette. Under Appearance , enable Atom and bond ambient occlusion . Adjust AO strength from 0–100%; zero restores the normal molecular view. Leave Automatic AO radius checked initially. Read the chosen neighborhood in AO radius (angstrom) . To tune the scale, uncheck Automatic AO radius. The manual slider starts at the current automatic radius and covers 0.25–50 Å in quarter-angstrom steps. Smaller radii emphasize nearby contacts; larger radii emphasize broader recesses. For a molecular surface, expand the saved SES or SAS in Surfaces → Molecular surfaces and set its opacity to 1 . Use built-in shading and enable Molecular surface ambient occlusion in Appearance. This separate switch uses matte Lambert shading to bring out pockets and clefts. See the 1AON surface comparison . Automatic radius is derived from the atom-coordinate extent. Molecular surfaces use a wider neighborhood than atoms and bonds. With both switches active, the readout shows both radii. Manual mode uses one radius. Camera movement can change the visible screen-space effect while the radius stays fixed. AO uses the visible scene to emphasize contacts and recesses. Offscreen geometry is not included. Turn it off if navigation becomes slow. AO controls last through Open within the session; restart/reload begins with AO off. PNG exports include the current shading. Atom colors and picking still work. Each switch affects its own visible geometry. Quantum fields, custom shaders and protein depictions keep their materials. Turning AO off releases its image buffers. If enhancement fails, a message appears and normal rendering stays available; disable/re-enable to retry. A lost graphics context requires reload/restart. Atom colours The Appearance → Atom colours widget identifies Built-in default (118 elements) or the palette file loaded this session. Colours file… opens a JSON palette. Reset to defaults restores the bundled colors. Biological Coloring → Element displays these element overrides; other biological color modes use their own legends. Two optional MatterViz palettes are supplied: Pastel is lighter with pale-pink oxygen and is recommended for AO; Muted has subdued colors with dusty-rose oxygen. They also live in the source checkout's palettes/ and tester ZIP's Palettes/ . Both cover elements 1–109; 110–118 keep built-in defaults. Their upstream MIT notice accompanies the examples. Accessible elements is an optional alternative evaluated with color-vision simulations. It changes H, C, N, O, F, Mg, P, S, Cl, Ca, Fe, Zn, Br and I; the other 104 elements keep their built-in colors. Load the file with Colours file… , then use Coloring → Element . The blue nitrogen and orange oxygen depart from conventional CPK colors. Some element pairs remain ambiguous; pick atoms to read their identities. Read the coverage and evaluation notes . Version 0.10.3 includes the file in its Palettes/ folder and bundled connector resources. The download also works with the older 0.10.2 palette loader. Write a partial palette { "format": "eigenvista-atom-colors", "version": 1, "colors": [ { "z": 6, "symbol": "C", "color": "#ff00aa" } ] } z (atomic number) selects the element. The optional symbol is checked as a typo guard; it never selects an element. Partial palettes are supported: unlisted elements keep defaults. Colors must be lowercase #rrggbb . The entire file is rejected for a wrong format/version, missing or empty colors, duplicate/out-of-range atomic numbers, an invalid color, or a symbol inconsistent with its atomic number. The current palette remains intact on rejection. Palette changes are session-only and do not make the molecular document unsaved; a fresh session uses the built-in palette. Background and PNG exports In the scene toolbar, Background color opens a color picker. The initial color is #e8edef ; Reset background color restores it. The choice is session-only and is not written into molecular files. Frame the view, adjust lighting/appearance, and wait for any requested field calculation to finish. Choose Export image for eigenvista-view.png with the selected opaque background. Or choose Export image with transparent background for eigenvista-view-transparent.png . Empty areas are transparent; antialiased edges and translucent surfaces retain fractional alpha. Confirm the download completed, then open the PNG in an image viewer or place the transparent version on your intended background. Both actions capture the current rendered viewport after zooming, resizing, or an idle period. Toolbar/status overlays are excluded. Exports additionally include scientific labels, measurement monitors and visible numerical keys in normal and transparent images. Transparent export leaves the selected background visible in the app. Exports include the current field mode and AO; they are images, not saved scientific documents. Use Save separately to retain data. If an export fails, its error appears without changing the molecular document; try the export again. PNG files use the app or browser’s download mechanism. Check that the file has finished downloading before closing the window. Custom surface shaders See the illustrated shader guide for X-ray and cutaway views, downloadable presets and a complete worked example. The Appearance → Surface shader widget optionally replaces built-in surface materials with a vertex/fragment GLSL pair. It affects surfaces, not atom/bond AO. Shader sources and uniform values last for the session and are not stored in .eigenvista . Choose a Vertex shader and a Fragment shader file. The picker accepts .vert , .frag , .glsl , or text files. Optionally load a Parameters file ( .params ) with default uniform values. Choose Apply to : all surfaces or one saved surface. Click Apply shader . Parsed uniforms appear as live controls. Their edits redraw immediately. Choosing new source files leaves the previous applied pair active until you apply the new pair. Use Save parameters to export the current uniforms as a Molekel-style .params file. Desktop opens a save dialog; the browser downloads it. Cancelling is harmless; a write error appears in the panel. Use Clear shader to restore Diffuse/Blinn-Phong, clear loaded files/parameters, and reset shader transparency. Examples are included in the tester/source packages under Shaders/ ; repository examples also live in app/shaders/ and shaders/ . Classic GLSL 1.x built-ins such as ftransform() , gl_Vertex , gl_Normal , and gl_Color are mapped onto the current rendering environment. Surface colors feed gl_Color . Parameters and validation Matching uniform types retain their values when new sources load; changed types reset to defaults. A parameter file with a nonnumeric value, unsupported/mismatched kind, or wrong component count is rejected with its parameter name and line number, preserving current values and the applied shader. Clear before loading another pair when shared uniform types conflict. Parameter export uses lines such as float name TAB value and writes a complete replacement file. Transparency and errors Shader transparency starts checked and blends fragment alpha even when document opacity is 100%. Uncheck it for opaque rendering: final alpha becomes one and depth writes are enabled. It updates an applied shader live and is saved in neither the document nor parameter file. Clear shader resets it to checked. Compile/link errors appear in red in the panel after Apply. Correct and reapply the pair, or Clear shader to restore built-in materials. Transparent objects use ordinary object sorting; intersecting layers can show ordering artifacts.

title: Orbitals, densities, and fields
description: Select Molden molecular orbitals and electron density, render Cube scalar grids, and control isosurfaces, raycasting, volumes, resolution and mesh caching.
text: This guide follows EigenVista 0.10.5. Use the four tabs in the single Tools pane: Molecule, Fields, Surfaces and Appearance. The 0.10.5 Mac package includes this workspace and all the scientific-inspection tools described here. Find your way around the current workspace → Render orbitals and densities from Molden or native documents, or open a cube to visualize a sampled scalar field. Use a raycast or volume preview to explore the field, and generate an isosurface mesh when you want to save its geometry. Choose a field In Fields → Quantum fields , select under Orbitals , Density matrices , or Sampled fields . Only one field is active for volume/raycast preview. Orbitals come from supplied coefficients; density matrices come from the document or the reported occupation-derived Molden interpretation . A cube supplies scalar samples without orbital coefficients. Try bicyclic-c7h10.molden for the molecular orbitals and density shown in the gallery, or complex-field.cube for a 29-atom structure with a sampled scalar grid. The flask-shaped example menu beside Molecular data offers Hydrogen pair and Fractional open shell : mathematical demonstrations, not calculated molecular reference results. Opening an example replaces the current document after an unsaved-change confirmation. Orbital values use bohr^-3/2 ; density controls use electrons per bohr^3 . Imported grid scalar units remain unspecified: consult the producer rather than guessing from a label. A positive/negative orbital surface represents field sign, not positive/negative electrical charge. Generate a saved surface for one field Select the field in Fields → Quantum fields. Under Fields → Field rendering , enter a finite positive Isovalue magnitude. Generation attempts both the positive and negative level; only nonempty results are added. A nonnegative density may therefore yield one positive surface. Choose Grid resolution . The default is 40³ . Presets offer 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96, 128, 160, 192, 224 and 256 points per axis; use a custom positive integer for another resolution. These cubic labels describe the full grid. Click Generate surfaces . Sampling, signed meshing, and validation run in the background. The button becomes Cancel while work is active. On success, inspect the result in Isosurface mesh . Adjust colors/opacity, manage meshes under Saved surfaces , then Save to retain them on disk. An isovalue outside the sampled range can legitimately produce no surface. Try a smaller magnitude or another field. Larger resolution costs more CPU time and memory and is not an accuracy guarantee. Changing the selected field, isovalue, or resolution does not automatically regenerate existing meshes. For a sampled preview without mesh extraction, choose Volume preview or Sampled raycast preview under Mode . Analytic orbitals/densities are sampled directly; you do not need to generate a mesh first. Browse and generate several orbitals Click Orbitals (count) , such as Orbitals (24) for the water example. Its tooltip is Browse and select orbitals . Inspect the table: one-based row, label, spin, occupation, energy in hartree, and saved-mesh count. Missing numbers show -- , not zero; unspecified spin is Unknown . Use Search orbitals to filter by row number, label, identifier, or spin. Check individual rows. The header checkbox selects/clears the currently listed rows; filtering preserves checked rows outside the current list. Clear orbital selection clears every check. Set positive Isovalue and Grid resolution , check the orbitals you want, then click Generate selected . The window closes and progress identifies each orbital and its batch position. On complete success, all new meshes appear together in Isosurface mesh . Save when ready. Batch results are applied only after the entire batch passes validation. Cancellation or a recoverable error retains prior surfaces. Only checked orbitals' meshes are replaced; meshes of other fields remain. Multi-selection creates separate orbital meshes, not a combined orbital or a new density matrix. The Saved column counts meshes in the document's memory, including hidden meshes. It does not mean the document is on disk. Checkboxes are temporary and are not saved. Each opening of the orbital browser initially checks only the active orbital, when the active field is an orbital. Closing without generating leaves the document/settings unchanged. After a successful batch, the previous active orbital remains active if it was checked; otherwise the first checked orbital in document order becomes active. Its sampled preview is ready. The checks do not select multiple simultaneous volumes. Three rendering modes Mode What is drawn When work occurs Isosurface mesh Saved positive/negative triangles. Generate surfaces or Generate selected creates/replaces meshes. Reopened saved meshes draw immediately without recalculation. Sampled raycast preview Isovalue crossings found by rays through the current display grid. Preparing a field/resolution may sample it. Isovalue changes redraw the current sampled preview directly without regenerating saved meshes. Volume preview Accumulated color/opacity along rays through one display grid. Preparing a field/resolution may sample it. Switching between volume and raycast reuses the current grid. Sampled previews use an in-memory grid. Cube/stored-grid fields prepare it automatically on Open or selection. Analytic orbital/density fields sample when a sampled mode is requested, including after reopening a document. No marching cubes runs unless you explicitly generate surfaces. In sampled modes, selecting another field or changing resolution prepares a new preview while preserving the chosen mode and every saved mesh. Failure/cancellation retains the previous completed preview, field, and resolution. A failed preparation can be retried by selecting the mode, field, or resolution again. In mesh mode, selecting an analytic orbital changes the active field without calculation; choose a sampled mode or Generate surfaces to display it. Stored grids also prepare a preview when selected in mesh mode. The selected field's saved meshes are visually replaced by the sampled display. Other fields' meshes may remain visible. Eye/trash controls affect meshes, not a transient volume. Return to mesh mode when checking those controls. Sampling quality is different from grid resolution In either sampled mode, Sampling quality offers Draft , Standard (default), and Fine : 1, 2, and 4 samples per voxel-distance along a ray. Quality redraws the existing grid without a worker calculation, new meshes, or scientific-data changes. It does not mark the document unsaved. The choice continues across mode switches, is hidden in mesh mode, and is not saved. Fine can reduce missed crossings between display steps; it cannot recover details missing from the grid or guarantee detection of tangencies. Increase grid resolution only when you actually need a different grid and can afford the calculation. Cube fields: already sampled data Open .cube / .cub to obtain atoms, automatic display bonds, and one scalar grid. A new cube starts in Volume preview ; raycast is available immediately. Generate surfaces when you want portable saved geometry. No Gaussian basis, coefficients, or density matrix is required. The complex-field example contains 29 atoms and an 84 × 84 × 84 grid , with values between 0 and 1. Start at an isovalue of 0.65 and adjust it to explore the field. Follow the cube tutorial to compare the three modes. Accepted cube profile The file must contain one finite scalar per grid point, positive axis counts of at least two, finite bohr coordinates, and a nonsingular affine grid. Skewed and reflected grids are supported; axes need not align with Cartesian directions. Atom numbers 1–118 and zero-atom grids are accepted. The atom-row charge value is validated but not retained as a separate property. Ordinary and Fortran D/d numeric exponents are supported. A negative atom count denotes a standard orbital/dataset header with exactly one dataset ID, not a unit change. That ID labels the sampled field; it does not supply orbital coefficients. Optional NVAL must be one. Multiple datasets, negative axis counts/alternative coordinate units, ghost atoms, singular grids, and missing/extra samples are rejected. Export one field per cube with supported units; do not remove markers to bypass the profile. Scalar meaning/units remain unspecified even for an orbital-labelled cube. If the normal initial isovalue is at or above a nonzero field's peak magnitude, import can choose one tenth of that peak as a starting display value. This is reported and does not normalize the data. All-zero grids have no nonzero isosurface. Grid resolution bounds the display/meshing grid: a larger source can be downsampled while preserving its affine extent; a smaller source is not upsampled. Increasing the control cannot add missing source detail. The complete original f64 samples and affine grid are retained and saved alongside generated geometry. Progress and cancellation While work runs, Field rendering remains expanded when visible. A global activity strip keeps Cancel calculation reachable even when you change tabs, close Tools or enter Zen. Read the current field, orbital/batch position, phase, counts, and elapsed time. Sampling reports completed z slices and a per-field percentage. Meshing reports completion of the two signed passes, not progress within each cell pass. Preparation, transfer, and validation are indeterminate. Percentages restart for each phase and field; they are not a percentage of the whole batch. There is no remaining-time estimate. A single slice or meshing pass may take longer than another, brief phases may finish before they appear, and cached fields skip sampling. A phase label staying visible is not by itself a failure. Cancel terminates the current calculation and retains previous completed meshes/preview. The app runs one scientific operation at a time; other queued work, such as file conversion, continues in order. Batch cancellation does not publish a partial set. If work is too expensive, retry with fewer orbitals or a lower grid resolution. Density cost also depends strongly on basis size. Caching, replacement, and saving For unchanged scientific inputs, the most recently sampled field at the same resolution can be reused for another isovalue or appearance change. Sampling another field/resolution replaces that transient cache. Active calculation cancellation or a worker failure that restarts the worker clears it. Saved meshes are independent of the cache. Generate surfaces replaces that field's saved meshes, retaining other fields. A mesh records the isovalue actually used to generate it, even if the control is edited later. Save separate documents to keep multiple isovalues of one field. Colors/opacity can be changed without resampling; changing the isovalue does not silently change stored geometry. Native Save retains analytic inputs, original imported grids, and completed meshes with generation metadata. It does not save the transient analytic calculation/display grid, active mode, camera, sampling quality, or orbital checkbox selection. A reopened document with meshes starts in mesh mode. Stored grids rebuild previews from their saved source; analytic fields can be sampled again directly when you select a sampled mode. Memory and numerical precision Original imported scalar values are f64; current display textures and meshing use f32. A finite source grid that overflows f32 produces a preview/meshing error rather than silent clamping. Its valid document, bonds, and existing meshes remain open and savable with the authoritative f64 grid. This differs from a malformed import, which leaves the previous document open. Grid presets through 256³ are convenient starting points, not a maximum. EigenVista attempts the requested allocation for custom analytic grids, imported samples and saved geometry. It does not impose fixed memory, grid, basis, orbital or mesh quotas, or silently lower resolution to make a request fit. At 256³, one field has 16,777,216 samples : 128 MiB of f64 calculation values plus 64 MiB of f32 display values, before meshes, copies, and graphics memory. Save before large calculations. Recoverable errors preserve prior work; browser, driver, or operating-system termination can still lose unsaved work. Resource What can prevent completion Files, calculation arrays and saved results A real allocation failure, address-space exhaustion or an unrepresentable size/index. Numerical evaluation Unsupported scientific inputs, nonfinite results or insufficient floating-point precision for the requested coordinates. 3D previews and image export The graphics device's actual texture/framebuffer capabilities or an unsuccessful graphics allocation. Read the reported error before changing a request. A graphics-device constraint can prevent a 3D preview even when numerical data remain valid and exportable. If memory allocation fails, close unneeded results or retry with an explicitly smaller calculation. Progress and cancellation remain available during background generation; only you choose a lower resolution or coarser molecular-surface spacing. Rendering limits Raycasting can miss narrow features or tangencies between grid samples. Use Fine sampling quality for a smoother preview, or increase grid resolution to sample the field more densely. For imported cube data, detail is limited by the source grid. Volume depth comes from accumulated visible opacity. Opaque objects test that representative depth, but volume color integrates the whole ray; intersections may include color from behind an atom or mesh. Interpenetrating transparent objects use ordinary object sorting and can show ordering artifacts. Shrinkwrap and a transfer-function editor are not available.

title: Biological structures
description: Inspect PDB, mmCIF and BinaryCIF structures with chain colors, component filters, residue ranges, traces, tubes, ribbons and protein cartoons.
text: This guide follows EigenVista 0.10.5. Use the four tabs in the single Tools pane: Molecule, Fields, Surfaces and Appearance. The 0.10.5 Mac package includes this workspace and all the scientific-inspection tools described here. Find your way around the current workspace → Open PDB, mmCIF, or BinaryCIF with chain, residue, and atom identities to use Molecule → Molecular data → Biological structure . Try the public 1AON complex and compare the real application images in the gallery . What the importer selects The reader retains the first model/structure, common atoms, and one alternate conformer per residue, choosing the alternate with the highest mean occupancy. Zero-occupancy atoms are omitted. Unknown mmCIF element symbols are skipped with a notice rather than guessed. These policies can make displayed counts differ from the deposited source; read Import report and Provenance . Selected atoms can retain atom names and residue membership; residues retain chain, name, label/author numbering, insertion identifiers, observed segment, component kind, and deposited secondary assignment. mmCIF label, author, and entity identifiers remain separate. PDB TER boundaries are respected and missing entity identifiers are not fabricated. Classification uses supported deposited component/polymer information and recognized names; unknown classifications remain explicit. mmCIF nonpolymer rows without label sequence numbers use author residue/insertion identity to distinguish waters and ligands. Different monomer names at the same sequence position can both remain selected. Protein paths break at that ambiguous position rather than selecting an invented conformer; inspect it in an atomic view or with a named residue range. Connectivity and source losses PDB CONECT and supported mmCIF/BinaryCIF covalent, disulfide, and metal declarations are retained, including accepted links beyond automatic distance cutoffs. Coordinate-based display connections fill gaps. Source declaration details and unresolved, duplicate, or omitted links are recorded in Provenance. Different/unknown symmetry images are reported without generating mates. Occupancies, B-factors, and formal charges are not retained as atom attributes; the complete source hierarchy and all annotations/models/conformers are not preserved. Cell/symmetry reporting is not crystal-image expansion. The importer supports a defined format profile, not complete mmCIF dictionary validation. Gzip input is supported only for BinaryCIF, not compressed text mmCIF or PDB. Keep the original structure file. Secondary assignments Supported PDB HELIX/SHEET and mmCIF/BinaryCIF deposited annotations supply secondary structure. Missing, unsupported, ambiguous, or conflicting assignments remain unknown with notices. EigenVista does not run DSSP or infer secondary structure from coordinates. An unassigned loop indicates missing assignment. Coloring and identity Choose Coloring under Biological structure. The legend explains the visible categories. Mode Meaning Element The CPK element palette, including any Atom colours override . Use this to see MatterViz Pastel with atomic AO. Chain Distinct deposited chain instances. mmCIF label identifiers appear with author identifiers when different; PDB uses author chain identifiers. Entity Chains belonging to the same supplied entity share a color. The supported PDB profile lacks this mapping and reports entity unknown. Secondary structure Deposited helices, sheets, and supported coil/turn assignments; unknown/unassigned residues remain gray. Residue class Colors standard protein residues by side-chain class: nonpolar, polar uncharged, acidic, or basic. Unclassified protein residues appear gray. Nonprotein atoms use element colors. Chain/entity colors are deterministic. Names/colors are based on the complete imported source, so filtering does not rename or recolor the remainder. Extra source identifiers distinguish otherwise identical displayed names in legends, controls, and picking. Unknown identities are labelled instead of inferred from location. A long legend shows its first 50 entries with a count notice. Click an atom to inspect element/index/angstrom coordinates with its biological context beside them. Selection does not resize the scene. Components, chains, isolation, and focus Expand Components . Show or hide the protein, nucleic acid, ligand, water, ion, and unknown component kinds actually present. Expand Chains (count) . Use Filter chain or entity to find an entry, then its checkbox to show/hide it. Long lists show at most 50 entries at once; filter to reach another chain. Use a chain's Isolate button to display that chain. Isolation restores the target chain's needed component visibility and clears a conflicting residue range. The button becomes Stop isolating ; activate it to remove isolation. Use Focus for a chain's visible atoms, or Focus visible structure to frame the full visible subset. Focus is disabled when no target atoms are visible. Choose Show all components to clear component/chain visibility, isolation, and residue-range filters and recover the full selected structure. Chain and component visibility filters combine: showing a chain alone does not override a hidden component kind except when isolation explicitly restores it. The chain text filter controls the list, not the molecular subset. If a structure seems absent, Show all components and Fit scene provide a useful reset. Protein depictions and style overrides The global Representation menu offers Protein backbone trace , Protein smooth tube , Protein ribbon , and Protein cartoon , alongside the atomic Ball and stick, Liquorice, and Van der Waals choices. Trace/tube follow supported backbone continuity; the secondary-structure cartoon distinguishes helical ribbons, strand arrows, and connecting loops. Component/chain style selectors use the shorter labels Backbone trace , Smooth tube , Ribbon , and Secondary-structure cartoon for the same protein choices. For an overview, choose Protein cartoon globally and Coloring → Chain . In Components or Chains, use an entry's style selector to give it a representation override. For example, keep the protein overview while inspecting a ligand or one chain in an atomic style. A chain override takes precedence over a component override; otherwise the global representation applies. Select Use global representation to remove that entry's explicit override. Choose Coloring → Secondary structure to inspect supplied assignments, and use chain isolation/focus for a closer look. Protein depictions are unavailable for nonprotein components, which keep atomic detail. Nucleic-acid cartoons and glycan depictions are not implemented. Missing data stays visible as a limitation Missing backbone atoms, source chain/segment ends, sequence breaks, and unsupported gaps break a path rather than bridge it. Ambiguous residue identities also interrupt the depiction. Ribbon and cartoon modes show missing assignments as thin unassigned loops. Residue-class coloring tints these loops by side-chain class. Other coloring modes show them in gray. Missing carbonyl orientation uses a thin-tube fallback and an informational notice; isolated backbone points remain visible as markers. Protein depiction geometry uses its own diffuse shading. Ambient occlusion continues to shade atomic spheres/bonds, not the new protein geometry. For an AO view of a dense complex, choose Van der Waals, Element coloring, and the Pastel palette. Show a deposited residue range Expand Residue range and choose the target Chain . Enter First residue and Last residue using deposited identifiers. Author numbering is used when supplied. Names are optional: ALA 10 through GLY 10A , or 10 through 10A , can include an insertion residue 10A . Choose Show residue range . The range is displayed and necessary component visibility restored. Use Clear residue range to remove just the range filter, or Show all components to clear all structure filters. Invalid, reversed, or ambiguous identifiers report an error and leave the previous selection intact. Use residue names where needed to distinguish deposited alternatives. Identifiers are source identities, not an invented continuous sequence: missing residues are not reconstructed. Session settings and saved metadata Coloring, component/chain styles, visibility, isolation, residue range, and focus are session display settings. They do not modify molecular data, resample a quantum field, or mark the document unsaved. Opening another file resets structure-specific selections and styles; the color mode continues when that file has biological metadata. Restart/reload resets these settings. The global representation remains a document setting and is saved. Native Save preserves selected biological identities when available. Such files need the biological-structure format feature and cannot be opened by older applications that lack it. Older native files remain readable, but identities discarded by their original importer cannot be recovered from them: reopen the original PDB/mmCIF/BinaryCIF to obtain current metadata. Chain and protein views use the biological metadata imported from PDB, mmCIF, or BinaryCIF. When the file lacks the required metadata, the app explains which views are unavailable. See saving and compatibility for sharing a document.

title: Scientific inspection
description: EigenVista scientific-inspection manual: select atoms, measure geometry, inspect ligand neighborhoods, create SES/SAS surfaces and analyze scalar fields quantitatively.
text: EigenVista 0.10.5 · Scientific inspection. The 0.10.5 Mac download includes the four-tab workspace and the scientific-inspection controls described here, through both the GUI and its bundled AI connector. It also includes visible atom picks, automatic field-plane updates and detailed molecular-surface progress. If you are using an older app, update it before following these workflows. Go from a molecular picture to a scientific observation. Select the atoms, measure their geometry, inspect molecular shape, and put numbers on a field. A true C₇H₁₀ HOMO section, with the controls used to make it: signed amplitude, contours and a continuous −0.06 to +0.06 bohr⁻³ᐟ² key. Open Fields, collapse Quantum fields and Field rendering when you want more room, then expand Quantitative field inspection. Actual 0.9.0 source-preview capture, 17 November 2026; this pane design became the default in 0.10.0 and is retained in EigenVista 0.10.5. Capture provenance . Find the new controls Pane tab Expand this widget Use it for Molecule Selections and measurements Ordered picks, named sets, monitors, labels and individual-ligand neighborhoods. Surfaces Molecular surfaces Coordinate-derived SES/SAS shape with an explicit radius table, probe and spacing. Fields Quantitative field inspection Field meaning/units, numerical probes, planes/contours and line profiles. The Tools pane starts 480 px wide on the right; its Position control moves it left. Resize the divider, collapse or drag widgets within a tab, or close Tools to recover the scene. Show tools or Shift+T reopens it without losing drafts. Zen and browser fullscreen are separate. Workspace and keyboard guide → The same operations are available to your external AI assistant . Request a scientific result in ordinary language. There is no requirement to learn programming commands, operate a file picker for the agent, or enter a model key inside EigenVista. Select source atoms in a useful order Enable Pick atoms for inspection and click atoms, or enter the viewer's atom numbers. Numbers shown to you start at 1. The ordered list has earlier/later and remove buttons. Filtering a chain or changing a representation keeps the original atom identities. Focus selection frames a set; Show only selection isolates it; Show full structure clears conflicting visibility filters. Save a Named selection when you want to reuse the same atoms for a neighborhood or molecular surface. Renaming or deleting a set never changes the loaded coordinates. Active picks/highlights are temporary and reset when another source is opened. Named sets are saved with the document. A saved set refers to its original atoms, rather than silently rebinding to similar labels in a different molecule. Visible picking cues in 0.10.5. Gold hollow reticles identify selected atoms. With selection picking off, a normal click shows a cyan ring at the inspected atom or bond endpoints without replacing your selection. Gold takes precedence for atoms already selected. Markers identify source-atom positions, including behind scene geometry; they do not trace atom or molecular-surface boundaries. Hidden atoms stay unmarked. Clear selection removes both cues; opening a new source resets them. Exported PNGs include the markers. Measure and annotate Distance: two distinct atoms; readout in Å. Angle: three atoms, centered at the middle atom; readout in degrees. Signed torsion: four ordered atoms; right-handed convention from −180° inclusive to below +180°. Pick order matters.
