Choose the kind under Geometry measurements , pick the required atoms and choose Add measurement . Edit the name, input order, kind, color or placement later. Hide a monitor to keep its definition without showing it on the figure. These are nonperiodic measurements of the supplied source coordinates. Distinct coincident atoms have zero distance; a zero angle arm or degenerate torsion plane is explicitly Undefined , with a reason. The app does not invent a zero or an uncertainty estimate. Atom and residue labels adds sparse text to a chosen target. Depth-aware labels follow scene occlusion; the always-visible option is useful for a presentation figure. Labels and measurement monitors are included in opaque and transparent PNGs. Export measurement CSV keeps names, ordered inputs, values, units and undefined statuses. Choose one ligand copy, then its environment In Ligands and neighborhoods , search the ligand list and choose a particular copy. Chain, residue number, insertion code and displayed residue number distinguish same-name copies. Choose a radius, optionally Include complete residues , then Show neighborhood . Give the result a name to retain it. The radius is an inclusive atom-center distance from the seeds to all loaded source atoms, including hidden atoms. Seeds remain included. Whole-residue expansion includes all atoms of a matched residue, even if some lie outside the radius; it requires biological identity metadata. The view resets conflicting filters before focusing the result. This is geometric proximity, not a hydrogen-bond assignment, affinity score, functional-pocket prediction or periodic crystal contact calculation. Distinguish SAS and SES A solvent-accessible surface (SAS) traces the solvent probe's center around atomic spheres. A solvent-excluded surface (SES) follows the molecular boundary accessible to the rolling probe, including reentrant shape. They need coordinates and radii, not a wavefunction. Choose all source atoms, the current selection or a named selection. All includes hidden atoms. A subset is calculated as an isolated object : omitted atoms no longer occlude it. It is not a cropped patch of the full-molecule surface. Choose Bondi / Mantina or Alvarez radii and explicit probe radius/grid spacing in Å. Radius overrides are available. Missing element radii cause an explicit error; choose a supported table or supply an appropriate radius rather than expecting a generic fallback. Display spheres and covalent-bond radii are separate inputs. Smaller spacing produces finer geometry and needs more memory. Cavities are kept; spacing is not silently coarsened. Generation has progress and cancellation, and regeneration replaces a cached mesh only when successful. Saved controls retain source/probe/radii/engine provenance, visibility, color and opacity. Opaque SES and SAS can use matte ambient occlusion with built-in shading. X-ray and clipping shaders retain their own lighting. Expand a saved surface to change its color and opacity immediately, without applying settings or regenerating its mesh. Use Rename surface to commit a name separately. Empty or out-of-range opacity input keeps the last accepted appearance; the generation form's initial color and opacity apply when generating a mesh. For a clear SES overlay, choose Ball and stick or Liquorice . Van der Waals spheres share the SES contact boundary; their independently triangulated surfaces can cross and produce patchy interference. Opacity does not separate those boundaries. Generation preserves your chosen molecular representation and display radii. A molecular-shape surface is not electron density or electrostatic potential. Save retains its cached mesh without requiring its original input file or another calculation on reopen. Live molecular-surface progress in 0.10.5. The surface controls and workspace activity display show the phase and elapsed time. During mesh generation, a bar shows completed blocks and the current phase's percentage. Other phases show activity without guessing overall completion or remaining time. The bar can restart when the phase changes. Progress and Cancel calculation stay visible when Tools is hidden or Zen is active; cancellation retains the previous accepted surface. Your external AI assistant can report the same status. Give a field an honest meaning Open Fields → Quantitative field inspection , choose the analysis field and expand Field meaning and units . Known analytic orbitals/density matrices have their supported interpretation; cube values remain unspecified until a meaning is supplied. Knowing the coordinate unit or filename does not identify the scalar quantity. An orbital section shows the signed amplitude ψ : positive and negative values identify phase. Total electron density ρ = Σ n i |ψ i |² is nonnegative and uses density units. Choose the total-density field for a density section; changing a label or colormap does not square an orbital. Spin or difference densities can have either sign and must retain their own meaning. Apply field meaning records a user declaration. Declaring source units labels the existing values without rescaling them. Supported Display and export unit conversions change readouts/keys/CSV while keeping raw samples intact. Orbital sign colors represent phase, not positive and negative charge. Read points, planes and lines A Point probe uses an entered coordinate or one selected atom. Plane / contours uses XY/XZ/YZ or three ordered atoms, with explicit width/height and columns/rows. The first atom centers the plane, the second defines its horizontal direction, and the third fixes its orientation. Collinear choices are rejected. A Line profile uses two endpoints or two ordered atoms, includes both endpoints and plots distance in Å. Coordinate inputs accept Å or bohr. Values come from direct analytic evaluation or interpolation of the original scalar grid, independent of the 3D preview's resolution. Skewed/reflected grid axes are preserved. Outside-domain samples are visibly missing, not zero-filled or extrapolated; profiles have gaps and contours do not bridge invalid cells. Use View meshes and analyses when a 3D volume hides a slice. This changes the viewing mode without generating a mesh. Existing saved meshes keep their own visibility; hide them separately if needed. Return explicitly to volume/raycast when you want that preview again. Each result supports Edit sampling , Recompute , visibility, label, colormap and range choices. A fixed range is useful for comparisons; Automatic sampled range restores the sampled range. Enter comma-separated plane Contour levels , then Apply result settings . Automatic plane updates in 0.10.5. A newly created plane stays open for editing with Auto-update plane enabled. Use a sampling spinner or its arrow keys; press Enter after typing a value. Orientation changes update it too. Rapid changes use the newest valid definition, keeping the previous complete plane and contours visible while work runs. Turn automatic updates off to edit several values before choosing Recompute analysis . Use Cancel plane update or Cancel editing to stop pending automatic work; collapsing the widget or hiding Tools keeps it running. Coordinate display-unit changes alone do not resample. Use Show numeric key for a quantitative slice's continuous colorbar. Show current field rendering key is different: it identifies the actual signed isovalues of mesh/raycast or the two-color volume's opacity transfer. It does not invent a continuous linear scale for those modes. Zen gives the same molecular section the full window while retaining its quantitative key and contours. Exit Zen or Tools returns to the pane; hiding controls does not change the analysis. Actual 0.9.0 source-preview capture, 17 November 2026; this pane design became the default in 0.10.0 and is retained in EigenVista 0.10.5. Capture provenance . Numerical samples and provenance and Export analysis CSV keep coordinates, values/units, domain status, method and source identity. CSV reports coordinates/profile distances in Å and values in the chosen display/export unit. Finite numerical data can remain inspectable/exportable when a particular 3D depiction reaches its graphics-precision limit; read the displayed explanation. Keep the scientific result Save retains named selections, label and measurement definitions, SES/SAS meshes with provenance, and accepted numerical definitions, caches, interpretation and local appearance. Reopening restores cached fields and meshes without silently recomputing them. Use the current 0.10.5 app; these document capabilities were introduced in 0.10.0 and are not readable by older 0.8.0 packages. Camera, active pick mode, biological filters, palette, background, AO and custom shader settings remain session choices. Save the document and export the figure separately. PNGs include scientific labels/monitors/visible keys; toolbar/status overlays stay out. Plan larger calculations EigenVista attempts the requested allocations for molecular meshes, named sets, annotations, numerical samples and exports, without fixed memory or item-count quotas. Larger grids and finer surface spacing can require substantially more memory and time. Generation runs in the background with progress and cancellation; recoverable allocation failures retain earlier accepted results. Requested spacing, cavities and source atoms are preserved. The app does not silently coarsen a surface, shorten a numerical result or discard warnings to make it fit. If your computer cannot allocate a request, choose an explicitly smaller extent/count or a coarser spacing and retry. Actual address-space/index representation, floating-point precision and graphics-device capabilities still apply; read the reported cause . Try it Measure and annotate → Compare SES/SAS → Inspect an orbital quantitatively →

title: Measure, label and keep the geometry
description: Select a real C7H10 bond, measure distance and torsion, export labelled figures and tables, then extend to ligand neighborhoods.
text: EigenVista 0.10.5 · Scientific inspection. The 0.10.5 Mac download includes the four-tab workspace and the scientific-inspection controls described here, through both the GUI and its bundled AI connector. It also includes visible atom picks, automatic field-plane updates and detailed molecular-surface progress. If you are using an older app, update it before following these workflows. A figure should tell you which atoms were measured and keep the numbers that support it. Start with one real carbon–carbon bond, then reuse the same selection. The first two carbons of the 17-atom C₇H₁₀ example are about 1.525 Å apart. The bridge-carbon label targets atom 7; annotations are exported by the app. Actual pre-release app export; original proportions retained. Capture provenance . 1. Open the example Use EigenVista 0.10.5 and bicyclic-c7h10.molden . This is the same calculated example used by the orbital tutorials. For this lesson you need only its geometry. Preserve the input and use new names for output files. Choose Ball and stick . If a volume obscures the atoms, expand Fields → Quantitative field inspection and choose View meshes and analyses ; hide any saved surfaces separately. 2. Measure the C–C bond Open Molecule → Selections and measurements . Enter 1, 2 in the atom-number box and choose Select atom numbers . Alternatively enable picking and click those atoms in order. Expand Geometry measurements , choose Distance , name it C–C bond , and choose Add measurement . Check a value near 1.525 Å in the table and scene monitor. Rotating/zooming must not change it. Checkpoint: the monitor measures the original coordinates. It does not estimate a distance from the picture or depend on the display sphere radius. 3. Keep selection and pick order separate Save the two atoms under Named selections as Measured bond . Then try four ordered atoms 1, 2, 7, 3 for a connected carbon-path torsion. Choose Signed torsion and add a separate monitor. Read its signed value rather than assuming a planar structure. Use the earlier/later buttons to change pick order before creating another measurement. A saved monitor retains its own ordered inputs. Undefined geometry is reported explicitly; do not copy it as a numeric zero. 4. Make an annotated figure Expand Atom and residue labels , choose atom 7 , and enter Bridge carbon . Choose a readable color and decide whether the label should respect depth or remain visible. Keep annotations sparse enough to avoid overlap. Frame the molecule and export a normal or transparent PNG. Open the actual image and confirm that its label/monitor is present and legible. Choose Export measurement CSV , then Save a new measured-c7h10.eigenvista . Reopen the native document and confirm the named set and monitor definitions remain. Reapply camera/palette/shader session choices separately. 5. Extend the idea to a binding-site neighborhood With the 1AON example , expand Ligands and neighborhoods and choose a particular ADP copy using its chain/residue identity. Start at 4 Å , include complete residues, name the neighborhood and choose Show neighborhood . Hidden source atoms are searched too. Whole residues can extend beyond the radius because one atom brought their residue into the set. This is proximity, not a hydrogen-bond or affinity assignment. Use the new named set as a later surface input. Ask your agent instead Use EigenVista 0.10.5 and the C7H10 example. Measure the distance between atoms 1 and 2, label atom 7 as the bridge carbon, and save an annotated transparent image, a measurement table and a new native document. Check the actual exported files and preserve the input. Your agent handles the connection and file operations; you do not need programming commands or manual GUI steps. Follow the installed-app connection guide first, using the compatible Mac package named there. Next Compare molecular surfaces → Measurement reference →

title: Compare solvent-accessible and excluded shape
description: Generate genuine SES/SAS molecular surfaces with explicit radius tables, probe and spacing, compare views and retain cached geometry.
text: EigenVista 0.10.5 · Scientific inspection. The 0.10.5 Mac download includes the four-tab workspace and the scientific-inspection controls described here, through both the GUI and its bundled AI connector. It also includes visible atom picks, automatic field-plane updates and detailed molecular-surface progress. If you are using an older app, update it before following these workflows. A molecular surface answers a geometric question about atoms and a solvent probe. Keep those choices explicit, and compare SAS with SES without confusing either with electron density. C₇H₁₀ SES with Bondi/Mantina radii, a 1.4 Å probe and 0.15 Å spacing, shown with an X-ray finish. This is coordinate-derived molecular shape, not an electron-density isosurface. Actual pre-release app export; original proportions retained. Capture provenance . 1. Start with a manageable structure Open bicyclic-c7h10.molden in EigenVista 0.10.5. Its 17 atoms make a quick first comparison; the surface needs their coordinates/radii, not the file's quantum fields. PDB/XYZ/mmCIF structures can use the same controls. Choose View meshes and analyses to remove a sampled volume, and hide unrelated saved quantum meshes. Keep the atomic framework visible. 2. Generate the first SES Choose the Surfaces tab and expand Molecular surfaces . Choose Solvent excluded (SES) , all source atoms, and Bondi / Mantina radii. Start with a 1.4 Å probe and 0.5 Å spacing. Name the surface and choose Generate molecular surface . Wait for completion and inspect the saved surface's scientific provenance. It should echo your kind, radii, probe and actual spacing. Smaller spacing gives finer geometry. To obtain the illustrated finish, generate or regenerate explicitly at 0.15 Å after the first test succeeds. No automatic coarsening is used. Cancellation/error retains the earlier accepted mesh. 3. Compare SAS using the same inputs Keep the SES, choose Create a new surface , and select Solvent accessible (SAS) with the same atoms, radii, probe and spacing. Give it a different name. Toggle visibility so you compare one surface at a time from the same camera. SAS follows the probe center, while SES includes the probe-contact/reentrant molecular boundary. A difference is expected. It does not establish a charge distribution, functional pocket or interaction energy. Compare like-for-like settings before interpreting geometry differences. 4. Understand selected surfaces Choose Current selection or a named set when inspecting a local object. The calculation treats only those atoms as an isolated object: omitted atoms cease to occlude the surface. It is not a window cut out of the full molecule's existing mesh. For a large protein, first select/name the intended chain or ligand neighborhood. Your agent can resolve the source identities and prepare the set for you. A small selected surface is often a more useful first test than requesting an entire assembly at very fine spacing. The same Surfaces widget on the left: 327-atom crambin with a solvent-excluded surface, Pastel atoms and the X-ray finish. This is a separate protein example, not the C₇H₁₀ surface above. Actual 0.9.0 source-preview capture, 17 November 2026; this pane design became the default in 0.10.0 and is retained in EigenVista 0.10.5. Capture provenance . 5. Reveal the interior and keep the result Choose Ball and stick or Liquorice to avoid the coincident-contact interference of Van der Waals spheres with SES. Expand the saved surface and change its color or opacity: the view updates immediately, with no Apply button or mesh regeneration. Use opacity or the X-ray/clipping surface shaders to reveal the framework. Choose the particular molecular surface as the shader target if you want other meshes untouched. Save a new c7h10-shape-comparison.eigenvista and export the figure. Reopen it and confirm both cached shapes and their provenance load without regeneration. Camera and custom shader settings remain session choices, so keep the exported figure too. 6. Reveal pockets with ambient occlusion Set a saved SES or SAS to opacity 1 and use built-in shading. Open Appearance and enable Molecular surface ambient occlusion . Leave Automatic AO radius on to scale the effect with molecule size. Uncheck it to tune the radius, or adjust AO strength to soften the shadows. AO OFF AO ON Reveal molecular surface AO 50% Full 1AON SES, 4.18 million triangles, from the same camera. Alvarez radii, 1.4 Å probe, 0.5 Å grid spacing and 24 Å automatic AO radius. Download 1AON . If a radius or allocation is rejected Some elements lack a value in a selected table. The app names the missing element; choose a suitable table or provide an explicit positive radius with defensible provenance. Do not silently omit it or substitute a display radius. Generation attempts the requested allocation without a preset memory ceiling. If allocation fails, choose an explicitly coarser spacing or smaller source selection and retry; the error does not silently change your settings. Ask your agent instead Using EigenVista 0.10.5, compare solvent-excluded and solvent-accessible surfaces for the complete C7H10 example. Use Bondi/Mantina radii, a 1.4 angstrom probe and 0.25 angstrom spacing. Keep both cached meshes, show one at a time from the same camera, apply the X-ray finish only to the SES, and save two images plus a new native document. Report the actual settings and any radius or memory errors. Next Put numbers on an orbital → Surface reference →

title: Inspect an orbital quantitatively
description: Probe a real HOMO, sample a true plane with contours and a fixed numerical key, plot a bond profile and export the values.
text: EigenVista 0.10.5 · Scientific inspection. The 0.10.5 Mac download includes the four-tab workspace and the scientific-inspection controls described here, through both the GUI and its bundled AI connector. It also includes visible atom picks, automatic field-plane updates and detailed molecular-surface progress. If you are using an older app, update it before following these workflows. A colored surface suggests shape. A probe, slice and line profile tell you what values are actually there. C₇H₁₀ HOMO (MO 26), z = 0 bohr: 14 × 12 bohr plane, 192 × 192 samples, fixed ±0.06 bohr⁻³ᐟ² range and contours at −0.04, −0.02, +0.02 and +0.04 bohr⁻³ᐟ². Actual pre-release app export; original proportions retained. Capture provenance . 1. Select a field with known provenance Open bicyclic-c7h10.molden in EigenVista 0.10.5. Expand Fields → Quantitative field inspection and choose the example's HOMO, MO 26 , as the analysis field. Inspect Field meaning and units : this is the real orbital amplitude ψ , with values expressed in bohr⁻³ᐟ² under the supplied basis/coefficients. The signs are orbital phase, not positive and negative charge. Total electron density is a different, nonnegative field, ρ = Σ n i |ψ i |² , in electrons/bohr³. This tutorial samples the supplied HOMO; it does not calculate a new wavefunction or a density from its color. 2. Read one source point Choose Point probe . Enter a coordinate with an explicit Å/bohr choice, or select exactly one atom and choose selected source atoms. Create the result and inspect its numerical value, unit and sampling method. Moving the camera or changing 3D preview resolution must not change the number. Analytic Molden fields are evaluated directly; imported cube fields are interpolated from their original samples. These are different methods and are identified as such. 3. Make the illustrated plane Choose Plane / contours and coordinate units bohr . Choose XY , center 0, 0, 0 , width 14 and height 12 . Set 192 columns and 192 rows , label it HOMO section , and create the analysis. Choose View meshes and analyses if a sampled 3D field hides it. Hide unrelated saved meshes separately. Under the result, disable automatic sampled range and set −0.06 to +0.06 . Choose the blue/white/red colormap and enable its numeric key. Enter contour levels −0.04, −0.02, 0.02, 0.04 and choose Apply result settings . Checkpoint: you see a true sampled plane with a fixed amplitude key and contours, not a clipping plane through a 3D isosurface. Tilting the view makes that distinction clear. For a local molecular frame, pick three noncollinear atoms and choose Three selected atoms instead. The first centers the plane, the second defines its horizontal direction, and the third fixes the orientation. A plane aligned to atoms is not automatically an orbital nodal plane. 4. Plot a profile along the measured bond Select atoms 1, 2 in order. Create a Line profile from selected atoms with 257 samples . Both endpoints are included, and the distance axis should span approximately 1.525 Å . Read the values and any sign changes rather than interpreting only a hue. Use Numerical samples and provenance to page the accepted values. Export analysis CSV keeps coordinates/profile distances in Å, values in the selected display/export scalar unit, and method/source information. A profile is not a line integral or a bond-order calculation. 5. Apply the workflow to an unknown cube field The 29-atom cube example contains an 84 × 84 × 84 scalar grid, with sampled values between 0 and 1. Its supplied meaning/units are unspecified. You can probe, slice, contour and export numerical values without inventing an identity such as electron density or ELF from the filename. Declare a meaning only when you have producer provenance. Outside the finite grid, a probe is marked outside, a plane has missing regions and a profile has gaps. Those samples are not zeros or extrapolated values. Finer interpolation does not add information to the original grid. 6. Save a reproducible numerical result Export a PNG with its visible numeric key and save a new native document. Reopen it to confirm definitions, accepted numerical caches and interpretation survive without silent recalculation. Use a fixed range for comparisons and record the camera/session choices separately. Ask your agent instead In EigenVista 0.10.5, inspect the HOMO of the C7H10 example. Make an XY section centered at the origin, 14 by 12 bohr with 192 by 192 samples. Use a fixed amplitude range from minus 0.06 to plus 0.06 and contours at plus and minus 0.02 and 0.04, with units visible. Also plot 257 values along the bond between atoms 1 and 2. Save an image with the key, both numerical tables and a new native document. Preserve the source and verify the saved outputs. Continue Quantitative reference → More ordinary-language requests →

title: Your first molecule
description: Open a PDB or XYZ file, inspect automatically generated bonds, rotate and zoom the molecule, and save a portable EigenVista document.
text: This guide follows EigenVista 0.10.5. Use the four tabs in the single Tools pane: Molecule, Fields, Surfaces and Appearance. The 0.10.5 Mac package includes this workspace and all the scientific-inspection tools described here. Find your way around the current workspace → Get ready You need the installed Mac preview and water.pdb . The alternative water.xyz gives the same 3-atom, 2-bond check. These files supply geometry, with coordinates in angstroms. No quantum-chemistry program is needed. Outcome: a water structure you can navigate and inspect, saved as a new .eigenvista document. 1. Open and check water Launch EigenVista. If the initial mathematical example is visible, click Open and choose the downloaded water.pdb . If asked about changed content, save anything you want to keep before replacing it. Choose Molecule and expand Molecular data if necessary. Check 3 atoms and 2 bonds . The importer computes display connectivity even when an input does not supply explicit connections. Open Molecule → Provenance to see import decisions. Then choose Fields → Quantum fields : it should say No quantum fields . The imported document remains unsaved until you explicitly Save. Checkpoint: you can see one oxygen and two hydrogens. The two bonds are generated automatically from the atom positions. 2. Move and inspect Left-drag in the scene to rotate. Right-drag or Ctrl-drag to pan. Scroll to zoom, or use the viewport’s Zoom in and Zoom out buttons. On a touchscreen, one finger rotates and two fingers pinch or pan. Click an atom. The status below the scene identifies its element and index and shows coordinates in angstroms. To create an actual distance or angle, use Molecule → Selections and measurements in a matching current build; see the measurement lesson . Click Fit scene to restore the default framing and direction. You can Tab to toolbar buttons and activate them with Enter or Space. Checkpoint: the atom and bond counts stay the same while you navigate. If the molecule leaves the view, Fit scene brings it back. 3. Change the representation Under Molecule → Molecular data → Representation , try Ball and stick , then Liquorice . Choose Van der Waals for space-filling spheres. Bond cylinders disappear in this representation; the document still contains its two bonds. Return to the representation you want to keep. A representation change marks the document as changed. 4. Save and reopen Click Save . Choose a new filename such as my-water.eigenvista in the native destination dialog and finish saving. Preserve water.pdb . Click Open and choose your new .eigenvista file. Confirm that it still has 3 atoms , 2 bonds , and the representation you saved. Use Fit scene if needed. Camera position is not saved, so reopening does not reproduce your exact viewing angle. Checkpoint: the native document is self-contained for the imported structure and connectivity. Save does not write PDB or XYZ, and opening an input never overwrites it. If something differs If the initial example is still visible, use the app’s Open button and select the downloaded file again. Finder file associations and drag-and-drop loading are not implemented. If counts differ, verify the filename and read Provenance and the error message. For an apparently empty view, try Fit scene and Ball and stick . Next, explore the hydrocarbon’s calculated orbitals to add quantum fields. For all navigation and appearance controls, see the scene reference .

title: Explore frontier orbitals
description: Open a Molden calculation, select HOMO and LUMO orbitals, compare volume rendering with isosurfaces, and save high-resolution meshes in EigenVista.
text: This guide follows EigenVista 0.10.5. Use the four tabs in the single Tools pane: Molecule, Fields, Surfaces and Appearance. The 0.10.5 Mac package includes this workspace and all the scientific-inspection tools described here. Find your way around the current workspace → A closer look at a hydrocarbon Download bicyclic-c7h10.molden and open it in EigenVista. This bicyclic C 7 H 10 molecule has 17 atoms , 125 basis functions and 118 orbitals . The first 26 orbitals are doubly occupied. You will explore its frontier orbitals, switch between volume and surface rendering, and keep a high-resolution mesh. The hydrocarbon’s HOMO, MO 26 (26a), rendered at ±0.03 bohr −3/2 on a 256³ grid. The two surface colors identify opposite signs of orbital amplitude. 1. Find the frontier orbitals Check Molecule → Molecular data for 17 atoms and 125 basis functions . Choose Ball and stick under Representation to keep the molecular framework visible. Choose Fields → Quantum fields and click Orbitals (118) . The orbital browser lists row number, label, spin, occupation and energy. Find row 26 , labelled MO 26 (26a) : the HOMO has occupation 2.000 and energy approximately −0.209458 hartree . Row 27 is the zero-occupation LUMO. Use Search orbitals if needed. Close the browser with Close orbitals and click MO 26 (26a) in the orbital field list to make it the active field. The browser’s checkboxes select orbitals for mesh generation; clicking a field row selects the field for a preview. 2. Explore the sampled field In the Fields tab, expand Field rendering . Set Isovalue to 0.03 and Grid resolution to 256³ to match the illustrations. A 128³ grid is useful for a quicker first exploration. Choose Mode → Sampled raycast preview . Wait for the field to finish sampling, then rotate and zoom to inspect its lobes. Switch to Volume preview and choose Sampling quality → Fine . The volume reuses the same grid; Fine increases the display samples taken along each viewing ray. Switch to Appearance → Appearance to choose positive and negative colors and adjust opacity. Keep enough contrast between the field, the atoms and the background to read the molecular framework clearly. Switching tabs keeps the current field and camera. The same MO 26 field in Volume preview, with isovalue 0.03 bohr −3/2 , a 256³ grid and Fine sampling. Raycast and volume previews use the sampled grid directly. Generate a mesh when you want to keep an isosurface as geometry, or apply a custom surface shader. 3. Keep a smooth signed surface Open Orbitals (118) , click Clear orbital selection and check row 26 . Keep Isovalue at 0.03 and Grid resolution at 256³ . Click Generate selected . Follow the sampling and meshing progress until the completed result appears. A matching sampled grid can be reused. The view switches to Isosurface mesh . Choose Surfaces → Saved surfaces and use the eye controls to view each signed part separately, or show both to see the complete orbital. For the illustrated finish, choose Surface shading → Blinn-Phong , set Opacity to 100% , Positive color to #75e1df and Negative color to #ffa1bc . Use #17232d for the background. Rotate and zoom until the cage and lobes fill the view. Try another isovalue to see how the orbital’s extent changes. Generating again replaces that orbital’s saved meshes; changing the control alone leaves the existing geometry intact. Save separate documents to retain several isovalues of one orbital. 4. Compare the HOMO and LUMO Hide the HOMO meshes under Saved surfaces , select row 27’s field in Quantum fields , and choose a sampled preview. Keep the camera, grid resolution and isovalue unchanged for a useful comparison. Look at how the lobes and their signs change around the same carbon framework. To keep both orbitals, check rows 26 and 27 in the orbital browser and choose Generate selected . EigenVista creates separate meshes for each orbital. Use the saved-surface eye controls to switch between their views. MO 27 (27a), the LUMO, at the same ±0.03 isovalues and 256³ resolution. Opaque surfaces give the two phases clear boundaries. 5. Save and take the view further Click Save and choose a filename such as c7h10-frontier-orbitals.eigenvista . Reopen it to display the saved meshes immediately, with the molecular and orbital data alongside them. Choose a sampled mode to prepare a volume or raycast again. Preview grids and camera framing are session choices; the saved mesh retains its generation isovalue and resolution. Use Export image or Export image with transparent background to keep the current view. For an envelope around the molecular framework, select Occupation-derived total density (listed orbitals) under Density matrices . Then try an X-ray finish or reveal the interior with a clipping shader. For numerical values and nodal contours, choose Fields → Quantitative field inspection . A true HOMO plane with a colorbar and contours complements the 3D surface. It measures signed amplitude ψ; choose the total-density field for nonnegative electron density. Next Shape the light with surface shaders → Measure a true HOMO section → If something differs If an orbital is hard to find, clear the search filter and use its row number. If Generate selected is disabled, check an orbital and enter a positive isovalue. For an empty surface, lower the isovalue magnitude or choose another orbital. Use a smaller grid for faster exploration; Cancel retains completed surfaces and the last completed preview.

title: Explore a cube field
description: Load a Gaussian Cube scalar grid, compare raycast and volume rendering, choose an isovalue, and save its original samples with an isosurface mesh.
text: This guide follows EigenVista 0.10.5. Use the four tabs in the single Tools pane: Molecule, Fields, Surfaces and Appearance. The 0.10.5 Mac package includes this workspace and all the scientific-inspection tools described here. Find your way around the current workspace → A field around a molecular complex Download complex-field.cube . It contains 29 atoms and an 84 × 84 × 84 grid: 592,704 scalar samples ranging from 0 to 1 . The source comments do not specify the scalar quantity or its units. You will explore this field with raycast and volume rendering, then generate a mesh and save it with the original grid. The imported field at isovalue 0.65, using its 84³ source grid and Fine raycast sampling. 1. Open and explore the grid Use Open to load complex-field.cube . Check 29 atoms under Molecule → Molecular data ; bonds are generated automatically. The field appears under Fields → Quantum fields → Sampled fields . After the initial preview is ready, set Grid resolution to 96³ . The app retains this smaller 84³ source grid at its original sampling. Under Fields → Field rendering → Mode , choose Sampled raycast preview . Set Isovalue to 0.65 and Sampling quality to Fine to match the illustration. Rotate and zoom to inspect the field around the atomic framework. Try isovalues between 0.65 and 0.75 to see how the boundary changes. Switch to Volume preview for a translucent view through the field. Both preview modes use the imported grid directly. 2. Keep an isosurface mesh Choose the isovalue you want to retain, or return to 0.65 . Keep Grid resolution at 96³ . Click Generate surfaces and wait for completion. Choose Isosurface mesh to inspect the stored geometry under Saved surfaces . Compare the mesh with Sampled raycast preview . Changing the raycast isovalue redraws the preview immediately; the stored mesh keeps the isovalue used to generate it. Generate again to replace the saved mesh with a different boundary. For a new finish, apply an X-ray or clipping surface shader to the mesh. 3. Save the field and the result Use Save to create complex-field.eigenvista . Reopen it with Open . The atoms, bonds, original scalar field and generated mesh remain together; the saved geometry is available immediately. Choose Volume preview or Sampled raycast preview to explore the stored field again, then export an image of your chosen view. The native document keeps the original samples and grid alongside the generated geometry. Camera framing and preview settings are session choices, so restore them when composing another view. Explore further Cube field reference → Large structures and ambient occlusion →

title: Read a large biological structure
description: Explore the 1AON mmCIF structure with MatterViz Pastel, molecular ambient occlusion, chain colors and protein cartoons, then isolate a subunit.
text: This guide follows EigenVista 0.10.5. Use the four tabs in the single Tools pane: Molecule, Fields, Surfaces and Appearance. The 0.10.5 Mac package includes this workspace and all the scientific-inspection tools described here. Find your way around the current workspace → Get ready Download 1AON.cif and matterviz-pastel.json . 1AON is a deposited GroEL–GroES chaperonin complex. This file imports 58,870 selected atoms , making it a useful example of broad molecular folds and crowded contacts. Read the data source and palette notices . Outcome: an atom-colored space-filling AO view, a chain overview, an isolated protein view, and a PNG of your chosen framing. This is a local graphics workload; allow import and scene preparation to finish before navigating. 1. Prepare the atomic view Click Open and choose 1AON.cif . Wait for the import to finish. Choose Molecule → Molecular data , check 58,870 atoms , and open Provenance in the same tab for model, alternate-location, and connection decisions. Set Representation → Van der Waals for space-filling atomic spheres. In Molecule → Molecular data → Biological structure , set Coloring → Element . This is necessary for the element palette to be visible instead of chain, entity, or secondary-structure colors. Choose Appearance → Atom colours , click Colours file… , and choose matterviz-pastel.json . Confirm that its filename replaces the built-in palette label. The lighter colors make shaded contacts easier to read. Click Fit scene . Rotate to a useful view of the complex, then leave the camera unchanged for the comparison. Checkpoint: you see atomic spheres colored by element with the Pastel palette. 2. Compare normal lighting and ambient occlusion In the Appearance tab, expand the Appearance widget and leave Atom and bond ambient occlusion off initially. Observe the contacts and central recesses. Optionally export this view before continuing. Enable Atom and bond ambient occlusion . Active AO uses Lambert shading plus SSAO , without specular highlights. Keep Automatic AO radius checked and read AO radius (angstrom) . Adjust AO strength while keeping camera, palette, representation, and background unchanged. Compare a moderate strength with zero, then toggle AO off and on. Zero or Off restores normal molecular rendering. For a closer experiment, uncheck Automatic AO radius . The manual slider starts from the automatic value: smaller radii emphasize nearby contacts; larger radii can emphasize broader recesses. Recheck automatic radius afterward. 1AON with normal molecular lighting and AO off. Both captures use the same camera, geometry, MatterViz Pastel palette, Element coloring, Van der Waals representation, and background color #ecebe4 . The matching view with Lambert shading plus SSAO at 100% strength and the automatic 14.25 Å radius. The difference includes the active mode’s matte material as well as its screen-space shading. Checkpoint: the shading changes while atom counts, connectivity, and element colors stay the same. The automatic radius comes from the atom-coordinate extent, so zooming does not change that radius. The visible effect can still change with the camera. AO emphasizes depth and contact regions by shading atomic spheres and bonds; hidden and offscreen geometry affect what the screen-space method can show. Turn it off if navigation slows. The gallery provides the paired captures for comparison. 3. Switch to chains and protein cartoons Set Atom and bond ambient occlusion off. Switch to Molecule → Molecular data , choose Representation → Protein cartoon , then Biological structure → Coloring → Chain . Use Fit scene to frame the complete complex. Expand Chains . Each row identifies a deposited chain instance. If needed, use Filter chain or entity to find the chain you want; the list displays at most 50 matching entries. For chain A, use Isolate , then Focus . Alternatively, Focus visible structure frames all currently visible atoms. A chain style can override a component style, and either can override the global representation. Choose Coloring → Secondary structure . Inspect deposited helices, strand arrows, and unassigned loops. Click an atom where atomic detail is visible to inspect its biological context. Use Show all components to clear isolation and visibility/range filters. Return to Coloring → Element and Representation → Van der Waals when you want the atomic AO view again. Chain coloring separates the subunits in the complete complex. Protein cartoon geometry has its own diffuse shading; molecular AO applies to atomic spheres and bonds. An isolated chain with deposited secondary-structure coloring. Unknown or unassigned regions remain explicit; EigenVista does not predict secondary structure. Checkpoint: isolation hides other chains without removing them from the document. Missing backbone atoms, chain boundaries, and unsupported gaps break protein paths rather than inventing connections. Nonprotein components retain atomic representations. 4. Export the view and save the data Choose your final representation, colors, and framing. To capture the shaded atomic view, restore Element , Van der Waals , the Pastel palette, and your AO settings first. Use the viewport’s camera button, Export image , for eigenvista-view.png . Or use Export image with transparent background for eigenvista-view-transparent.png . The PNG includes current scene shading and camera framing; toolbar and status text stay out. Exports also include visible labels, measurement monitors and numeric keys. Check that your host completed the download. Click Save and choose a new filename such as 1aon-study.eigenvista . This retains the selected molecular data, biological identities, connectivity, and global representation. Keep the original mmCIF file too. Session versus Save: AO, atom palette, background, biological coloring, chain/component style overrides, visibility, isolation, residue ranges, and focus are session settings. They are not written into .eigenvista . Camera framing is also not saved. Reload starts with AO off and the built-in atom palette; load Pastel and restore your display choices to recreate the illustration. A PNG captures the current appearance but is not a molecular document. Image export uses the host’s download mechanism. Confirm that the actual PNG arrived and inspect it before relying on it. If something differs If Pastel seems ineffective, choose Coloring → Element . If an isolated chain vanishes, use Show all components , check chain/component filters, and focus again. If AO reports an enhancement error, disable and re-enable it to retry; normal molecular rendering remains available. A lost graphics context requires a reload, so Save completed work first when possible. Continue in the biological structure reference for component styles and residue ranges, or the scene reference for palettes, backgrounds, and PNG export. Return to the learning path to explore calculated fields.

title: Shape the light
description: Apply custom GLSL shaders to molecular isosurfaces: create an X-ray finish, clip an electron-density surface, and adjust parameters live in EigenVista.
text: This guide follows EigenVista 0.10.5. Use the four tabs in the single Tools pane: Molecule, Fields, Surfaces and Appearance. The 0.10.5 Mac package includes this workspace and all the scientific-inspection tools described here. Find your way around the current workspace → Reveal the molecular framework through an X-ray shell. Cut into a density surface. Change the lighting, color and transparency while you explore. Watch the 30-second demonstration of these live controls → X-RAY / VIEW-ANGLE OPACITY GLSL SURFACE SHADER The X-ray shader emphasizes the surface silhouette while letting the molecular framework show through. CLIPPING / LOOK INSIDE LIVE PARAMETERS Move a clipping boundary to reveal the structure beneath the surface. The molecular model stays in place. Try it yourself Prepare a surface Give it an X-ray finish Cut into the surface Tune the view live Keep the result Download the presets Start with a molecular surface Custom shaders give you direct control over how an isosurface is drawn. Load a ready-made preset to get started, or bring your own vertex and fragment GLSL files. Choose Appearance → Surface shader in the single Tools pane for the editable controls. Open bicyclic-c7h10.molden and select its total density under Fields → Quantum fields → Density matrices . In the same Fields tab, expand Field rendering . Set Isovalue to 0.04 electrons/bohr³ and Grid resolution to 256³ , then click Generate surfaces . The images here use this same density mesh. Under Fields → Field rendering → Mode , select Isosurface mesh . Use Ball and stick to see the atomic framework alongside it. Frame the molecule with the rotate, zoom and Fit scene controls. For the complete field workflow, see the orbital tutorial . The shaders below work on the generated surface, so you can try several finishes on the same geometry. Give it an X-ray finish For the finish shown in Crambin in X-ray , load the bundled surface-x-ray.vert , surface-x-ray.frag and surface-x-ray.params from the package’s Shaders/ folder. Leave Shader transparency enabled and adjust the surface color to change the tint. This preset makes front-facing areas more transparent and keeps the outline stronger. It is useful when a surface would otherwise hide the atoms inside. Download x-ray.vert , x-ray.frag and x-ray.params . Choose Appearance and expand Surface shader . Use Vertex shader… for x-ray.vert and Fragment shader… for x-ray.frag . Use Parameters file… to load x-ray.params . Leave Shader transparency checked. Choose All surfaces under Apply to , or select an individual surface, then click Apply shader . For the illustrated finish, set maxOpacity to 0.85 , minOpacity to 0 and da to 0.03 . Use the toolbar’s background picker for #17232d . Rotate the molecule and adjust color to suit your view. Control What to try color Choose the tint of the shell. minOpacity Raise it to give front-facing areas more body; lower it to see more of the framework. maxOpacity Lower it to soften the strongest edges. da Raise this cutoff to remove the faintest parts of the shell and emphasize its contours. Keep minOpacity at or below maxOpacity . The preset’s eyePosition values start at zero; leave them there for the standard view. Cut into the surface Clipping opens a window into a molecular envelope. Six controls bound a visible box; move one boundary across the molecule to expose what it encloses. Click Clear shader before switching presets. Load surface-clip.vert , surface-clip.frag and surface-clip.params with the same three file buttons. Choose the target under Apply to and click Apply shader . Adjust xmin and xmax , ymin and ymax , or zmin and zmax . Keep each minimum below its matching maximum. Enlarge the bounds first if the surface is mostly hidden. For the illustrated cutaway, keep factor at 0.24 , set all bounds to −10 / 10 , then bring zmax to 0.25 . Set the surface’s Positive color to #93e8d9 . Rotate the view to inspect the exposed framework. The factor control scales the coordinates used by the clipping box. Its preset value is 0.24 ; leave it fixed while finding the six bounds for your molecule. For a solid finish, uncheck Shader transparency . Tune the view live The parameter names come directly from the shader. Numbers, checkboxes, vector components and color pickers appear as appropriate. Once a shader is applied, editing these controls updates the scene immediately: there is no need to generate the surface again. Adjust the finish while keeping the same molecular surface. Tour the current four-tab workspace . Open the controls at full size . This earlier 0.7.2 close-up illustrates shader parameters; find the current widget under Appearance → Surface shader. To switch the underlying shape, choose another field or isovalue and generate its surface. To change only the appearance, keep the geometry and adjust the shader. Clear shader returns to the built-in Diffuse or Blinn-Phong surface shading. Keep the result Use Save to keep the molecular data and generated mesh in an .eigenvista document. Click Save parameters in the shader panel to download your current settings as a .params file. Keep it with the vertex and fragment files; load all three to restore the finish in a later session. Use Export image for the current view, or Export image with transparent background to place it on a slide or figure. The molecular document stores the surface geometry; the shader files and saved parameters keep the appearance. See saving and sharing for the document details. Download the presets Finish Files Useful for X-ray Vertex · Fragment · Parameters See the molecular framework through a luminous surface silhouette. Clipped diffuse Vertex · Fragment · Parameters Expose an interior region with six editable clipping boundaries. More lighting and clipping examples are included in the application package’s Shaders/ folder. For accepted shader files, parameter handling and error messages, see the surface-shader reference . title: Ask your agent. Watch EigenVista.
description: Use Codex, Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode or another local agent to open molecules, change their appearance and export images in the installed EigenVista app.
text: Find an orbital, reveal a density surface, load a palette or focus on one protein chain. Tell your agent what you want and watch the same EigenVista window respond. EigenVista 0.10.5 groups manual controls in four Tools tabs: Molecule, Fields, Surfaces and Appearance. You can watch or adjust the scene while your agent works; scientific requests do not depend on which tab is open. The current 0.10.5 package includes the same scientific workflows. See the current workspace . Included in EigenVista 0.10.5 for Mac and Linux. The app ships its connection helper, launcher, agent instructions and examples together. Set up your agent and start exploring with ordinary prompts. Connect the installed app → What to ask your agent → RECORDED AGENT SESSION C₇H₁₀ / HOMO An actual app export from a recorded external-agent session: the C₇H₁₀ HOMO (MO 26), on a 128³ grid, with an X-ray finish. Follow the orbital workflow → Ask for the view you need [01] Explore orbitals “Find the HOMO and LUMO. Show both signs of the HOMO and explain what the colors mean.” Orbital walkthrough → [02] Look inside density “Show the electron density, then make the surface transparent enough to see the molecular framework.” Density walkthrough → [03] Bring out the depth “Load MatterViz Pastel and compare ambient occlusion off and on from the same angle.” AO walkthrough → [04] Read an assembly “Show a protein cartoon, color by chain, isolate chain A and focus on it.” Representation walkthrough → The app includes the connection tools Explore scientific inspection in 0.10.5. Ask for geometry measurements/labels, ligand neighborhoods, SES/SAS molecular surfaces, and quantitative field probes/planes/profiles. The 0.10.5 packages and their connectors include the core inspection workflows. It also includes visible atom picks, plane-update controls and detailed molecular-surface progress. Ask your agent to confirm available features when connecting to an older or custom app. A HOMO plane shows signed amplitude ψ; a total-density plane shows nonnegative electron density. Read the scientific-inspection manual → A compatible EigenVista package ships its connection helper, standalone agent instructions, launcher, examples and palettes together. You do not need a separate MCP plugin. Your agent reads those instructions and handles discovery, commands and progress checks. Use Codex Desktop or CLI, Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode , or another agent with local terminal and file access. Codex Desktop already has terminal access; its CLI is optional. An image viewer lets the agent inspect and show actual PNG exports. There is no chat box or model account inside EigenVista; you keep using your chosen agent. Two ways to get connected Manual setup : open the packaged launcher in Finder or Terminal, then give your agent the nonsecret setup note. One setup prompt : authorize your agent to find or download the compatible app, read its packaged instructions, start a session and check the connection. The launcher keeps your input folder between sessions and creates a fresh private results folder each time. It starts one new enabled window and leaves existing app windows alone. You choose which data folders the agent may use. Local viewer, chosen model Molecular processing and the connection to EigenVista run locally. Your external agent may still send prompts, file contents or images to its chosen model provider. Share only data you are allowed to send and keep credentials and the private connection file's contents out of chat and logs. For on-device-only work, choose an agent that supports a local model and check its tools, telemetry and network settings. OpenCode documents local runtimes ↗ . Configure the model in the agent; EigenVista does not install or manage one. Continue with your agent Next Installed-app setup → Everyday requests →

title: Connect the installed EigenVista app
description: Set up a connector-enabled EigenVista Mac or Linux package with its bundled launcher, or give your agent one prompt to install and connect it for you.
text: Use the connection tools already included in your package. Open its launcher yourself, or give your agent the setup prompt and let it handle the installation and connection. Use EigenVista 0.10.5 for Mac or Linux. Its connection helper, launcher, instructions, examples and palettes are included together. Download and install EigenVista , then choose the setup method below. Check the included files when using an older or custom package. Choose the agent you already use Your agent needs local terminal/file access and, to inspect exported pictures, an image viewer. A cloud-only chat without access to the computer running EigenVista cannot control its local app. Keep an existing working agent installation; choose only one if you need to install one.
